title: Porsche 911 Carrera 4 GTS Coupé
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 2011

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	One of the rarest modern 911s•	Circa 7,500 miles from new•	Full Porsche service history•	Exceptionally well-specifiedRepresenting a major step forward, the Type 996 version of Porsche's perennial 911 sports car - introduced in 1997 - really did justify its maker's claims to be 'all new'. With the 996's introduction, Porsche finally adopted water cooling for the flat-six engine, which remained behind the rear wheels of a car that shared no panels with its immediate predecessor and was longer, wider, and higher than before. Not surprisingly, given the Type 996's wholesale re-engineering, the successor Type 997 - introduced in 2004 - represented evolution rather than revolution, the most significant changes being to the interior and exterior styling. The latter marked a welcome return to the 911's traditional oval headlights, and the interior too was more classic 911 than that of the outgoing 996. The base 3.6-litre engine remained essentially the same as the Type 996's, while the more expensive 'S' models came with a more powerful 3.8-litre unit. There was also a new four-wheel drive system.For 2011, Porsche introduced the first-ever 911 to carry the designation 'GTS'. Conceived as a more road-usable alternative to the track-focused GT3, the GTS had 408bhp on tap, 23 horsepower more than the S version, while also featuring appropriately uprated suspension and race-inspired centre-lock wheels. Unique styling features included a Sport Design front bumper, special rear bumper, blackout trim, GT2-type side skirts, and 'Carrera GTS' door sills in brushed stainless steel. Alcantara trim was standard, but many GTS customers specified leather upholstery. In the January 2025 edition of 911 & Porsche World there was a lead 12-page feature on the 997.2 GTS. The 997 was described as 'the sweet spot of the modern 911 era, de facto modern classic, and why's it's the last of the 'enthusiast 911s', further claiming the GTS as 'the best of the 997 range' and that it could be the ultimate, liveable, everyday 911.First registered on 29th September 2011, this Carrera 4 GTS has had only two registered keepers, the present one since September 2022, and currently displays a total of circa 7,500 miles on the odometer. The car is finished in Aqua Blue Metallic with Sand Beige interior and comes with a data sheet listing its numerous optional extras, including Adaptive Sports Seats; Bose Surround Sound; Electric Sunroof; and Sport Chrono Package Plus. It has been serviced at Porsche Edinburgh and Porsche Glasgow throughout its life, at the following dates:28/1/2014 – Porsche Edinburgh18/9/2017 – Porsche Glasgow30/6/2021 – Porsche Glasgow12/9/2022 – Porsche Glasgow25/4/2025 – Porsche EdinburghDated May 2025, the most recent invoice is for just over £2,200 for maintenance work carried out by Porsche Centre Edinburgh. The current MoT certificate expires in September 2026.

title: Ferrari 458 Italia Coupé
provenance: Formerly part of a large private collection in Hong Kong
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 2010

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Formerly part of a large private collection in Hong Kong•	Purchased and brought to the UK by the vendors•	Recently resprayed (all bills and 'before' photographs available)•	All books and tools"Back in 2009 the Ferrari 458 Italia emerged from the famous factory gates in Maranello to replace the 430. Its ancestry reaches all the way back to the late '60s Dino, the car named after Enzo Ferrari's son that forged the concept of the 'junior Ferrari' and introduced the mid-engined platform to the brand." – evo magazine.Although officially announced as the F430's successor, the 458 was an entirely new design, incorporating technologies developed as part of the Italian manufacturer's Formula 1 programme. The 458's specification and performance suggested that it was anything but a 'junior' Ferrari, as it boasted a 4.5-litre V8 engine producing 562bhp, an output good enough for a top speed of 325km/h (202mph). Reflecting the ongoing trend among supercars towards clutch-less semi-automatic transmissions, a seven-speed Getrag gearbox of that type was the only one available on the 458. To the regret of many enthusiasts, Ferrari's classic gated manual 'box was no longer an option. In keeping with Ferrari tradition, the 458's body was designed by Carrozzeria Pininfarina under the supervision of Ferrari's design director, Donato Coco. As one would expect of a car with a 200mph-plus capability, aerodynamics played a major role in the design, yet despite generating considerable downforce the 458's beautifully curvaceous body was remarkably devoid of extraneous appendages. Former Ferrari Formula 1 driver Michael Schumacher had a hand in the design of the interior, which featured a steering wheel incorporating many of the controls normally located on the dashboard or on stalks, as found in modern competition cars.   Despite the apparent handicaps of 135kg weight disadvantage and regular road tyres, the 458 lapped Ferrari's Fiorano test circuit quicker than the track-focused 430 Scuderia. "This was the result of Ferrari going for gold in every department," declared evo. "The 458 represented a quantum leap in technological terms, bringing a hoard of new systems into play to create an enveloping, pure driving experience."Spin-off models were not long in coming, the first new 458 variant being the almost inevitable Spider, introduced in 2011. The Spider was followed in 2013 by the 458 Speciale, which offered even more performance than before. Revised bodywork and active aerodynamics were two of the many advances over the original 458, together with updated electronics and an engine that now produced 597bhp. In 2014 Ferrari introduced an open-top version: the 458 Speciale Aperta. Representing the model in its original coupé configuration, this right-hand drive Ferrari 458 Italia has come from a large private collection in Hong Kong where it was kept indoors together with its owner's 458 Spider, seeing minimal use. Purchased and brought to the UK by the vendors, the car had acquired some minor paintwork blemishes while in storage so was resprayed at a cost of circa £7,000 (see bills and 'before' photographs on file). Also on file are previous service invoices issued by the official dealer in Hong Kong together with some others issued since the car arrived in the UK. Offered complete with a V5C document, MoT to July 2026, and all books and tools, this beautiful modern Ferrari is presented in impressive condition throughout.

title: Ferrari 365 GT 2+2 Coupé
provenance: Formerly part of Ferrari UK's private heritage collection, known ownership history from new.
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1968

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Formerly part of Ferrari UK's private heritage collection•	Known ownership history from new•	Original colour combination•	Fastidiously maintained regardless of cost (bills available)•       Classiche certified•       Matching chassis and engine numbersBy the mid-1960s, 50 percent of all Ferraris produced were being built with four seats, and following on from the success of its first such model, the 250GTE of 1960, Ferrari introduced the 330GT 2+2 in January 1964. The newcomer's steel tube chassis was 50mm longer in the wheelbase than that of its predecessor and featured independent front suspension and a live rear axle, while beneath the 330's more-spacious Pininfarina coachwork was a 300bhp, 4.0-litre V12 coupled to a four-speed overdrive gearbox. Its replacement, the 365GT 2+2, was launched at the Paris Salon in October 1967. Sleekly styled in the manner of the limited edition 500 Superfast, the 365GT 2+2 was the most refined Ferrari to date. Based on that of the contemporary 330GTC, the chassis was made up of Ferrari's familiar combination of oval and round steel tubing, and as well as featuring independent suspension all round (for the first time on a Ferrari 2+2) boasted Koni's hydro-pneumatic self-levelling system at the rear. Further refinements included mounting the engine and drive-train with rubber bushes to insulate the car's occupants from noise and vibration, and providing ZF power-assisted steering and air conditioning as standard equipment. Developing 320bhp in its 365GT incarnation, the well-proven 4.4-litre V12 engine was coupled to a five-speed gearbox, while the car's blistering performance - top speed 150mph, 0-60mph in 7.0 seconds - was restrained by Girling ventilated discs all round. A total of 800 cars had been completed by the time production ceased in 1971, only 50 of which were right-hand drive.  Endowed with that unusual combination of fine handling and a supple ride, the 365GT 2+2 was rated by Car magazine as 'the most civilised Ferrari yet.' Right-hand drive chassis number '12025' was delivered new in the UK to Colonel Ronnie Hoare CBE, head of Ferrari importer Maranello Concessionaires, and displayed on the company's stand during the 53rd International London Motor Show at Earls Court (see supporting dealer/factory correspondence on file). In 1969 Maranello Concessionaires sold the car to one B F Bird, who traded in his Ferrari 330GT as evidenced by a copy of the original invoice and other correspondence on file. In 1977, the Ferrari was acquired by one M K Watsham, who kept it until 1983 when it was purchased by a Mr Samen. That same year, the car went to marque specialists DK Engineering for an engine rebuild and other restoration work. Between 2000 and 2002, '12025' resided in Ferrari UK's private heritage collection before being purchased from the immediately preceding owner by our vendor at Bonhams' Goodwood Revival sale in September 2009 (Lot 214). At that time the Ferrari was registered as 'MUD 200'. The purchaser in 2009 was Martin Kenwright, an interactive Academy Award winner and the creator of some of the world's biggest driving games, including the official WRC franchise on PlayStation alongside the other Sony PlayStation launch titles of MotorStorm and Drive Club. The Ferrari was bought as a genuine usable classic and has been driven only on short pleasure trips around the local village in beautiful North Wales, seeing relatively little use since acquisition. Stored in a heated private garage, the car has been exceptionally well looked after, receiving regular services and maintenance, including an engine overhaul. All minor mechanical and electrical jobs have been done, with comprehensive tweaks and fixes made over the years. The radiator has been reconditioned and the tyres are brand new, while one particular point of interest is the specially devised and developed shock absorbers, adjusted via a simple tyre hose in the boot.Between 2010 and 2013 the car was serviced by the JMH Automotive, and between 2015 and 2023 by Trevor Farrington in Knutsford. More recently, over £10,000 was spent on service and maintenance at specialist restorers Ramsport in Wales. One of the best-known Ferrari 365s in the UK, and the subject of numerous internet articles, '12025' is featured in A Guide to Ferrari Road Cars and comes with an extract from that publication. Fully documented, the car also comes with a Certificato d'Autenticità; all service records and expired MoTs dating back to 2002; and the all-important Ferrari Classiche certification. Finished in its original colour scheme of Tourbillon Blue with beige leather interior, this is a fully documented and properly maintained 365 GT 2+2, well suited to continued enjoyment and ready to please its fortunate next owner. In the vendor's own words: "I'll miss this car, it drives and looks great, and it's as honest as they come..."

title: Ferrari 365 GT4 Berlinetta Boxer
provenance: Delivered new in the UK, present ownership since 2004, part of the 'M' collection belonging to Dodi and Mohamed Al-Fayed.
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1974

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Delivered new in the UK•	Present ownership since 2004•	Extensive recent refurbishment"A racing Ferrari with a flat-12 engine first ran at Monza in September 1964, but the BB is the first production model to make use of this engine configuration. The Boxer's flat-12 is not a detuned racing 312P or 312 B2 or B3 unit as one might think. Rather, it's closer to the traditional 60-degree, four-cam, 4.4-litre V12 but flattened out to 180 degrees. The bore and stroke are identical and many parts such as pistons, connecting rods and valvegear are interchangeable." – Road & Track.Unquestionably one of the greatest cars Ferrari has ever built, the 365 GT4 Berlinetta Boxer debuted at the 1971 Turin Show in prototype form and commenced production in 1973 almost unaltered. An entirely new model and the first road-going Ferrari not to have a vee-configuration engine, the 356 GT4 reflected Ferrari's motor racing heritage; its 4.4-litre, four-cam, 'boxer' engine drew on experience gained from the Maranello firm's World Championship-winning, flat-12 F1 and sports-racing units and developed no less than 360bhp at 7,700rpm. Rumours abounded that the prototype Boxer had run at over 180mph, and even though the production version managed 'only' around 175mph, there can have been few disappointed customers. The mid-located engine gave near-perfect balance and ensured that the Boxer's handling matched its stupendous straight-line speed. A combination tubular/monocoque chassis housed the mid-mounted engine/five-speed transaxle package that ingeniously placed the motor above the gearbox and final drive, thus avoiding an overly long wheelbase. The ensemble was clothed in elegant, low-slung Berlinetta coachwork by Pininfarina. The result of extensive wind tunnel testing, Pininfarina's masterpiece was assembled at Modena by Scaglietti and comprised a superstructure mixing aluminium-alloy and steel panels, complemented by matt black-finished glassfibre elements beneath the front and rear overhangs. At the time of its introduction the 365 GT4 Berlinetta Boxer was the world's fastest and most expensive car. Only 387 were constructed between 1973 and 1976 and it remains one of the most desirable and sought after of all Ferraris. The example offered here is one of only 58 built in right-hand drive configuration out of 387 cars in total and thus one of the rarest of RHD Ferraris. Chassis number '17943' was completed on 27th May 1974 and delivered new to the UK Ferrari importers Maranello Concessionaires before being sold to H R Owen Ltd; it left the factory finished in Giallo Fly (yellow) with black Connolly leather interior trim. The car's UK registration was 'XMC 28M'. The Ferrari was regularly serviced and maintained by Maranello Concessionaires, Modena Engineering, S&H Motorsport and E G Autokraft and later became part of the 'M' collection belonging to Dodi and Mohamed Al- Fayed. The car was repainted red and re-trimmed in beige leather with black seat inserts, and in 1989 was seen at Modena Engineering in England. At some time its registration was changed to 'ASH 68'. In June 2004 the Ferrari was offered for sale at UK auction where it was purchased by the current vendor; at that time the odometer reading was stated to be 35,788 miles. On file is a list of maintenance works undertaken by our vendor between September 2004 to October 2009, together with another list of more extensive refurbishments undertaken in August 2025, which included engine-out replacement of the cam belts, tensioners and water pump (see invoices on file). Offered with a Massini Report; photographs of maintenance; copies of old MOT certificates from 1980-2003; and a documented  history with invoices from 1977-2004.Please note that this vehicle is from outside the UK. title: Maserati Bora 4.7-Litre Coupé
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1976

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	One of only 289 4.7-litre models made•	Rare right-hand drive version•	Present ownership since 1997•	Regularly serviced, maintained and MoT'dHighlight of the 1971 Geneva Salon was undoubtedly the sensational Maserati Bora. With the Bora's introduction, the great Modenese manufacturer followed other supercar constructors in going mid-engined while at the same time abandoning its traditional tubular chassis in favour of unitary construction. Named after an Adriatic wind, the Bora was the work of Giorgetto Giugiaro's Ital Design, at least as far as its bodyshell was concerned; the mid-mounted engine was Maserati's familiar four-cam V8 in 4.7-litre form, the five-speed transaxle came from ZF, and the all-independent double-wishbone suspension was penned by Giulio Alfieri, co-designer of the legendary 250F Formula 1 Grand Prix car. One of the first 'new generation' models to appear following Maserati's acquisition by Citroën, the Bora used the latter's hydraulics technology to adjust seats and pedals, raise the headlamps, and operate the excellent power-assisted brakes. A slippery shape plus 310bhp made for a very fast car - top speed was over 160mph - and the Bora had acceleration, handling and braking to match. The subsequent 4.9-litre version was even faster. The total produced was only 564, the 4.7/4.9-litre split being 289/235. Finally phased out during 1979, the Bora was a stunning supercar by any standards, both then and now. This right-hand drive Bora was acquired for £30,000 by the late owner in 1997, its keeper at that time being Mr Grenville Griffiths of Etchingham (from 1988). The previous keeper was Salma International Engineering Ltd of Bromley (1981), effectively the same owner as above (Griffiths). The Maserati had been advertised in Trident magazine as follows: "1976 RHD Bora, My ownership the last 16 years, one previously. Mechanically, bodily and interiorwise (sic) this is a virtually perfect Bora, truly unmarked and factory fresh. Jack Levy described it as the best Bora he has ever seen (Trident no. 63) 21,248 miles (yes, really)."Mr Griffiths had the Bora restored during his ownership, including a repaint from silver to dark metallic blue, and details and photographs are on file. A sum of circa £35,000 was spent on the rebuild. During the late owner's custodianship, regular maintenance, servicing and MoTs were carried out by Ferdi's Garage of Lytham, Lancashire from 1997 to 2018. Parts were obtained from marque specialists Bill McGrath Maserati. When the car was last MoT'd in 2018 the odometer reading was recorded as 22,514 miles and is now 22,556 (in 1986 when it was registered 'PUL 825R' the mileage was 20,517.

title: Lancia Dilambda 1st Series Sports Tourer
provenance: Delivered new to Australia, known ownership history, present ownership since 1985

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Delivered new to Australia and bodied locally•	Known ownership history•	Present ownership since 1985•	Continuously maintained while in the current ownershipCompleted on 1st March 1930, this Dilambda was exported to Melbourne, Australia and sold to Mr Anthony Barber on 3rd July 1930 by the Australian Lancia agents, Shields Motor Company Pty Ltd. The Lancia was then delivered to leading Melbourne coachbuilder, James Flood, who built the close-coupled sports tourer body that it retains today. Mr Barber was from a family of well known Lancia enthusiasts: the family also owned a Kappa and a couple of Lambdas.  He raced the Dilambda in a number of hill climbs in the early 1930s. Registration records show that the car passed through 10 owners and then to Mr Kim Brownbill, an Australian Lancia Register member, and then to Mr Ken Shine, from whom our vendor purchased it in 1985. Since 1985 the following significant work was done:( Refer to receipts for dates)Body bare-metal repainted in original colours with wheels and under-guards in red (all original panels and guards retained)Original sprung seats and door panels re-upholstered in Connolly hideRear carpet replaced. Wire wheels checked, renovated and reset, balanced by wire wheel expert.Mechanical overhaul in 1997-2000 and 2003 with various more recent work as required (see dates on receipts)Engine rebuildGearbox and differential rebuilt with new bearings, original gearbox gears re-lapped Clutch rebuiltBrakes, brake cables and rods, wheel bearings replaced, hubs, etcCarburettor renovated and jets replaced a number of times, including in 2024Most parts re-chromedKnock-ons and wheel hubs restored and re chromedSteering box and related mechanism restoredSprings and suspension, driveshaft and related bearings restored.Wiring repaired or replaced, coil replaced, distributor renovated with new points (original NOS Bosch platinum) Radiator replacedGenerator and starter motor rebuilt, battery replaced 2024Other components repaired as required.Original running boards restoredSpeedometer restoredNew tonneau cover (1997)New hood and hood cover (2017 )New tyres (two in 2013 and two in 2024 )New fuel pumpsOriginal scuttle wooden framework replaced and restored in 2013 to eliminate shake (steel panelling left intact)Original engine fan removed (included with the car) and replaced with an electric fanBody mostly taken back to bare metal, doors, etc repaired and realigned as required and repainted in 2024, again in original coloursOtherwise every effort has been made to retain originality. For example: the firewall, aluminium panels around the engine bay, dashboard, instruments and controls, manifolds and connections, etc are original. This car does not have side curtains. All early photographs show the car with the hood down and that is how the vendor drove it. Given the sporting predilections of the original owner, it seems unlikely he would have ordered side curtains or driven with the hood up. On the couple of occasions when the owner has driven the car in rain he found it quite dry and cosy in the front seat with the hood up and the tonneau fitted.The horn is activated by a button on the right of the dash. The original button on the wheel has a complicated connection via a carbon contact, which is unreliable. The one-shot lubrication system was disabled when the car was purchased. Former owners Messrs Brownbill and Shine both said it was messy and left oil patches under the suspension, etc. Lubrication is done using grease. The car has been well maintained by our vendor, including semi-annual oil changes and regular expert inspections, maintenance and tuning. An accompanying file details much of the maintenance records including regular tuning of the carburettor, spark-plugs and timing. The sliding pillar front suspension of many Lancia models, including the Dilambda, can suffer from wheel shudder if the wheels are unbalanced. This has been solved on this car by patient on-car wheel balancing, top quality tyres inflated to 40psi when warm, and with the recommended toe-in. The car has been used sparingly during the vendor's ownership, mostly on Lancia Register and VSCC Victoria rallies and has been on show a number of times, including at the Melbourne Motorclassica exhibitions in 2017 and 2024. According to the vendor: "This car handles well; I have kept up well with Aurelias, Fulvias and Flavias on difficult winding country roads during club events. The car handles city and heavy traffic well with good acceleration and excellent brakes."The body and fittings are original, as evidenced by the contemporary photographs of the car (originals held in the Australian Lancia Register archives)'; a letter from Lancia; the reference to the coachbuilder in the newspaper cuttings; and the bill of sale. The Lancia letter confirms the engine, gearbox and differential are original. The original owner's instruction handbook and parts catalogue are included in the sale. The car is currently registered in Australia and has a FIVA Identity Card; it is eligible for the Mille Miglia and other FIVA events. A file is included containing various contemporary and more recent articles on the Dilambda. title: Lamborghini Countach LP400S Coupé
provenance: Delivered new to a UK customer in Italy; Present ownership since 1999
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1981

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	One of only 237 built•	Delivered new to a UK customer in Italy•	Right-hand drive•	Present ownership since 1999•	Regularly serviced and MoT'dThe legendary Miura was always going to be a hard act to follow, so the extent to which its successor eclipsed the greatest of 1960s supercars came as something of a shock to all. The sensation of the 1971 Geneva Salon, the Countach was styled, like its predecessor, by Carrozzeria Bertone's Marcello Gandini. Looking aggressive from every angle, the Countach was nothing less than spectacular, suggesting it had been conceived on another planet. As it happened, the production version would not be seen for another three years, with deliveries commencing in 1974."...for sheer outlandish eye appeal, and track-car capability that's translatable for the road, there is simply no better car," declared CAR magazine. "It's hard, also, to imagine a better one coming along." But come along one did, in the shape of the much improved LP400S, which featured extensive alterations to the chassis and suspension to exploit the characteristics of Pirelli's newly introduced P7 tyre. "It corners at 180mph: we know, we've tried it," enthused CAR. The LP400S was built between 1978 and 1982, by which time 237 had been made. A ground-breaking design that set new standards for aspiring supercar manufacturers,  Lamborghini's Countach is one of the most iconic sports cars of the 20th Century, and all the more enjoyable in its uprated LP400S form.This stunning Countach LP400S was originally supplied in Italy to a UK customer and registered in Bologna on 12th November 1981 (the temporary Italian registration was 'EE 94194' expiring in November 1982). The keeper was Gerald David Pardo (originally from Egypt), who lived in London. The Countach was finished in Bianco (White) with red seats and black carpets.The late owner purchased the Countach from Pullicino Classics June 1999 at 727 kilometres for £56,000; it was described as 'unregistered, delivery miles, as new'. Today the odometer reading is c.2,700 kilometres. From 2000 to 2019 the Countach was regularly serviced and MoT'd by Ferdi's Garage of Lytham, Lancashire. In 2005 a new exhaust was installed via the London Stainless Steel Exhaust Centre Ltd (£1,700) while new tyres were fitted by Colin Clarke Engineering in 2018 at 1,200 kilometres. title: Ferrari 365 GT4 Berlinetta Boxer
provenance: Delivered new in the UK, present ownership since 2004, part of the 'M' collection belonging to Dodi and Mohamed Al-Fayed.
description_block:

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Delivered new in the UK•	Present ownership since 2004•	Extensive recent refurbishment"A racing Ferrari with a flat-12 engine first ran at Monza in September 1964, but the BB is the first production model to make use of this engine configuration. The Boxer's flat-12 is not a detuned racing 312P or 312 B2 or B3 unit as one might think. Rather, it's closer to the traditional 60-degree, four-cam, 4.4-litre V12 but flattened out to 180 degrees. The bore and stroke are identical and many parts such as pistons, connecting rods and valvegear are interchangeable." – Road & Track.Unquestionably one of the greatest cars Ferrari has ever built, the 365 GT4 Berlinetta Boxer debuted at the 1971 Turin Show in prototype form and commenced production in 1973 almost unaltered. An entirely new model and the first road-going Ferrari not to have a vee-configuration engine, the 356 GT4 reflected Ferrari's motor racing heritage; its 4.4-litre, four-cam, 'boxer' engine drew on experience gained from the Maranello firm's World Championship-winning, flat-12 F1 and sports-racing units and developed no less than 360bhp at 7,700rpm. Rumours abounded that the prototype Boxer had run at over 180mph, and even though the production version managed 'only' around 175mph, there can have been few disappointed customers. The mid-located engine gave near-perfect balance and ensured that the Boxer's handling matched its stupendous straight-line speed. A combination tubular/monocoque chassis housed the mid-mounted engine/five-speed transaxle package that ingeniously placed the motor above the gearbox and final drive, thus avoiding an overly long wheelbase. The ensemble was clothed in elegant, low-slung Berlinetta coachwork by Pininfarina. The result of extensive wind tunnel testing, Pininfarina's masterpiece was assembled at Modena by Scaglietti and comprised a superstructure mixing aluminium-alloy and steel panels, complemented by matt black-finished glassfibre elements beneath the front and rear overhangs. At the time of its introduction the 365 GT4 Berlinetta Boxer was the world's fastest and most expensive car. Only 387 were constructed between 1973 and 1976 and it remains one of the most desirable and sought after of all Ferraris. The example offered here is one of only 58 built in right-hand drive configuration out of 387 cars in total and thus one of the rarest of RHD Ferraris. Chassis number '17943' was completed on 27th May 1974 and delivered new to the UK Ferrari importers Maranello Concessionaires before being sold to H R Owen Ltd; it left the factory finished in Giallo Fly (yellow) with black Connolly leather interior trim. The car's UK registration was 'XMC 28M'. The Ferrari was regularly serviced and maintained by Maranello Concessionaires, Modena Engineering, S&H Motorsport and E G Autokraft and later became part of the 'M' collection belonging to Dodi and Mohamed Al- Fayed. The car was repainted red and re-trimmed in beige leather with black seat inserts, and in 1989 was seen at Modena Engineering in England. At some time its registration was changed to 'ASH 68'. In June 2004 the Ferrari was offered for sale at UK auction where it was purchased by the current vendor; at that time the odometer reading was stated to be 35,788 miles. On file is a list of maintenance works undertaken by our vendor between September 2004 to October 2009, together with another list of more extensive refurbishments undertaken in August 2025, which included engine-out replacement of the cam belts, tensioners and water pump (see invoices on file). Offered with a Massini Report; photographs of maintenance; copies of old MOT certificates from 1980-2003; and a documented  history with invoices from 1977-2004.Please note that this vehicle is from outside the UK. Our customs agents, CARS UK, will manage all post sale customs administration. A fee of £350+VAT will be charged on the buyer's invoice to administer both import or export customs movements. If the buyer also chooses to ship with CARS UK, this will be quoted separately. If this vehicle is to remain in the UK, it will be subject to Import VAT at the reduced rate of 5% on the hammer price. This vehicle will not be available for immediate collection after the sale and will only be released on completion of customs clearance formalities. title: Aston Martin DB6 Sports Saloon
provenance: The car has an unbroken history with documentation confirming ownership.
description_block:

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	The tenth DB6 produced•	Converted from automatic to five-speed manual transmission•	Engine rebuilt by Rikki Cann in 1997•	Used for extensive European touring•	Driven to the saleThe tenth DB6 produced, chassis number '2360/ R' was completed at the Newport Pagnell factory on 29th October, 1965 and delivered on 14th February 1966 to W H Benham (Bournemouth Limited). The guarantee form shows the car was ordered in Pacific Blue with black interior, and that it left the factory equipped with the following options: chrome wire wheels; heated rear screen; three-eared wheel spinners; and a Motorola radio with power aerial, all for a total price of £4,316. The Aston also comes with its original instruction book; a Heritage Trust Certificate; and an unbroken history with documentation confirming ownership. The DB6 was originally registered 'FEL 227C' to Mr and Mrs Loveday of Bickley, Kent, subsequently passing to Mr Ryder Ascott, also of Bickley, who covered some 30,000 miles in it. In 1973 the Aston passed to Mr G A Collis in Bromley, Kent, who added another 22,000 miles to the total. It remained with Mr Collis for some 20 years before being purchased by the present owner and AMOC member on 9th November 1993. The car remained registered in Belgium until 2015 when it was repatriated to UK, and has been in the present family's ownership for around eight years. The current odometer reading is 78,000 miles.While in Belgium, the Aston underwent a bare-metal respray in 1996 to dark green but retained its original black leather seats, original radio, and an eight-track cassette player. It was originally built with automatic transmission but was converted to a ZF five-speed manual gearbox in 1997, offering an altogether more sporting driving experience. At the same time, the engine was completely rebuilt at significant cost by recognised Aston Martin specialist, Rikki Cann. More recently, the brake callipers and brake lines were replaced; electric ignition fitted; and the carburettors refurbished and retuned. In addition, the engine has been 'topped and tailed' and a new floor fitted. The Aston's owner wanted a DB6 he could drive daily during summer months while his DB6 Vantage Volante was in build, and this car fitted the brief perfectly. Benefiting from regular usage and regular servicing by his in-house mechanic, this car has toured Europe - highlights being trips to the Spa Classic and the Mille Miglia - and is reported to have performed very well with no issues. The car will be driven to the auction, a distance of around 120 miles.An undervalued yet mechanically sound DB6, this 'oily rag' example is ready for a new owner to enjoy 'as is' or restore to a higher standard.

title: Bentley Azure Convertible
provenance: Offered for sale by Sir John Hall
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1996

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Offered for sale by Sir John Hall•	Specially commissioned by Bentley Motors Ltd•	Considerable recent expenditure on servicing and maintenance•	MoT'd to July 2026Hitherto, Bentley's resurgence had relied on models whose basic architecture was shared with other Rolls-Royce products; but also on display at Geneva in '85 was Project 90, a mocked-up coupé intended to gauge public response to the idea of a high-performance car unique to Bentley. When the real thing - the Bentley Continental R - was unveiled six years later, the waiting crowd burst into rapturous applause. In 1995 Bentley Motors announced a soft-top version of the Continental R, a full four years after the coupé's introduction. Once again, Geneva was chosen to launch what would turn out to be the first Bentley model in several decades to use an entirely new name - 'Azure' - which, like 'Corniche' and 'Camargue', evoked exotic destinations in the South of France. The famous Italian styling house of Pininfarina – a firm with unrivalled experience in the design of soft-top Gran Turismos – had been chosen to develop the Azure on the four-seater Continental R platform, and there was no questioning that the result was most successful. Bodyshells were assembled in Italy by Pininfarina, fitted with the automatic soft-top, painted and then shipped back for finishing at Crewe. Mechanically similar to the Continental R but with an engine further up-rated to 385bhp, the Azure cost £215,000 in the UK at time of launch. Hailed by its maker as, 'the world's best convertible', the Azure lived up to that grand title, proving an immense success especially in North America where its combination of unmatched luxury, effortless performance and soft-top style was found highly attractive. When production ceased in 2003 a total of 1,321 Azures of all types had been built. Finished in red metallic and a cream leather interior, this gorgeous Bentley Azure was delivered new to Sir John Hall, former owner and Life President of Newcastle United Football Club, and has covered a mere 5,700-or-so miles from new. A sill plaque is engraved: 'This vehicle was specially commissioned by Bentley Motors Ltd for the occasion of the Ruby Wedding Anniversary of Sir John & Lady Hall 28th July 1996'. As evidenced by invoices from Fearon Bentley Specialists, the car received an annual service and maintenance work to the alarm system and headlamp washer in June 2025 costing £4,235.75, and repairs to interior electrics in September 2025 costing £3,016.00. The Bentley is MoT'd until July 2026 with no advisories recorded. It should be noted that the HPI check notes two keepers, perhaps reflecting a change of registration from company to personal.

title: Porsche 911 Carrera 3.2-Litre Coupé
provenance: Over 20 years with the present owner
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1989

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Over 20 years with the present owner•	Extensive restoration by SSL in December 2021•	Very well specified from new•	In long-term storage for much of its life•	2nd in class at the 2013 Dolomite Classic Rally From the start of the 1984 model year, Porsche revived the evocative Carrera name for all 911 variants, co-incidentally with the introduction of the 3.2-litre engine. Although it remained an air-cooled 'flat six', the '3.2' was 80% new and incorporated an effective cam chain tensioner and associated lubrication system that at last addressed a perennial 911 shortcoming, including a long overdue upgrade to the earlier 915 transmission. An ECU controlled the fuel and ignition systems for the first time on a 911, enabling the engine to be both more powerful and less thirsty. As a result, this enlarged and extensively revised power plant now produced 231bhp, 27 horsepower up on its predecessor, endowing the Carrera with a level of performance approaching that of the original 911 Turbo of 1974, the bald statistics being a 0-60mph time of 5.3 seconds and a top speed of 152mph, with 100mph reachable in a breathtaking 13.6 seconds. Forty-plus years on, the Carrera 3.2 is now highly sought after and for very good reason, though finding one is not that easy. A final-year G-Series 911, this example is a C16 UK-supplied car, finished in its factory original Grand Prix White (L908) with a black leather interior (LT). Being a 1989 example, it does of course feature the desirable Getrag G50 5-speed gearbox and 16" Fuchs, rather than the standard 15" wheels as offered on previous models. Other important factory options include front and rear spoilers (473); sport shock absorbers (474); Blaupunkt Radio/cassette (330) and an electric sunroof (650).  This is the vendor's second Carrera 3.2 (his first was new in 1987) and has belonged to him for over 20 happy years. Initially he used the Porsche as a daily driver, which accounts for most of the mileage (just over 97,000), but more recently the car has been stored in the vendor's garage. It has been typically taken out on occasion for annual MoT testing and servicing, which thanks to its simplicity, was undertaken by the vendor.  In December 2021 the Porsche was restored following an earlier engine top-end rebuild by specialists JZM, that included new genuine Porsche front wings; inner/outer sills; kidney bowls; door posts; and light shells. The car in recent times been mechanically maintained by Jaz Porsche of St Albans, receiving new silencers; starter motor; distributor cap and pretty much anything else it needed. Redone only a few years ago, the paintwork still looks fresh, while the interior is described by the vendor as 'pretty impressive for 36 years old'.  In 2013 the Porsche was unexpectedly substituted for the vendor's usual rally car for the gruelling Dolomite Classic Rally. Heavily penalised for being a post-1983 car, but with legendary Works navigator Willy Cave on board, the Carrera achieved a shock result of 2nd in class against a field of very well driven European 911s.  This recently restored and very well cared for and hard to find wide-wheel Sport Coupe Carrera 3.2 comes with its original instruction manuals; a V5C document; current MoT certificate; and a comprehensive history file of restoration and servicing bills; expired MoTs; and sundry invoices.With the 3.2 emergent as the go-to for conversion houses building retrospective 2.7 RS replicas, the opportunity to acquire an original specification example represents an increasingly rare opportunity.

title: Ford Sierra RS500 Cosworth Group A Competition Saloon
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1987

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Rouse Sport car developed over many years•	Overall winner of the Silverstone Classic in 2017 and 2021•	Winner of the 2023 Silverstone Festival in Group A •	Fully refreshed since winning at Silverstone in 2023 (new block)•	Current FIA accreditation until the end of 2027•	Now eligible to the new HTC2 Peter Auto ChampionshipThe sight of rival manufacturers reaping the rewards of a successful circuit racing programme prompted Ford to renew its alliance with engine builder Cosworth to create the eponymous Sierra, assembly of the minimum 5,000 units required for Group A homologation commencing in June 1986 at the company's Genk plant in Belgium. Intended for circuit racing, the RS500 competition version was built by Aston Martin Tickford, with homologation completed in August 1987 after the 500 units required had been finished. Most of the changes from the road version were found in the engine, which featured a thicker-walled cylinder block; a larger Garrett T04 turbocharger; a larger intercooler; and an additional set of fuel injectors using the second fuel rail (unused in the production version). In addition, the fuel delivery, induction, and lubrication/cooling systems were up-rated, while aerodynamic alterations were made to the front and rear bodywork in the interests of increased downforce. According to the vendor, this Rouse Sport Ford Sierra RS500 is the definition of an 'on the button' race car having been constantly developed over recent years. Although this car has very limited in-period history it has enjoyed significant success in modern Group A competition, including overall victory in the 2017 Silverstone Classic event. Many fastest laps and pole positions have been achieved and most recently this example won the 2021 Silverstone Classic and the 2023 Silverstone Festival in Group A. This RS500 has been built and run to a high standard and has been fully refreshed since that win at Silverstone in 2023, The preparation has included a new cylinder block as part of a Harvey Gibbs engine build, together with new hubs, brake discs, a Ford Motorsport 909 differential, and a fully rebuilt Getrag 265 gearbox. Every Rouse suspension component has been removed, serviced and rebuilt. In 2023 £100,000-plus was spend at Melliard before going to Premier Motorsport for the latest specification suspension setup. In summary: one could spend many tens of thousands of pounds developing these cars to get them to this one's level of competitiveness and, importantly, reliability. The beauty of this particular example is that the current owner has already gone through that timely and costly process, meaning that this race-winning RS500 is now ready for its fortunate next owner to enjoy some of the best Historic motor sport in Europe, including the new HTC2 Peter Auto Championship. The car has current FIA accreditation until the end of 2027.

title: Lamborghini Jarama S Coupé
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1973

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	One of only 150 Jarama S models made•	Left-hand drive•	Desirable manual transmission model•	Present ownership since 1980•	Regularly serviced and maintained (bills available)Launched at the 1970 Geneva Motor Show and named after a region of Spain famous for its fighting bulls, the Jarama would be the last of Lamborghini's front-engined road cars for many years. Powered by Lamborghini's 4.0-litre quad-cam V12 engine, this new 160mph four-seater abandoned its maker's  existing spaceframe chassis in favour of a platform-type unitary construction, based on the Espada's but of shorter wheelbase. An unusual styling feature was the nose with its quadruple headlamps partially obscured by electrically raised covers. The Jarama was styled at Carrozzeria Bertone by Marcello Gandini, the man responsible for the Miura, but with bodies assembled by Marazzi. An improved 'S' version, with 365bhp V12 engine, appeared in 1972, while later developments included Torqueflite automatic transmission and power-assisted steering. The Jarama continued in production until 1976, by which time 327 cars had been built, 150 of them to 'S' specification. A desirable manual-transmission model, this left-hand drive Jarama 'S' was acquired by the late owner in May 1980 at 57,000 kilometres, the previous keeper listed being Burmah Castrol c/o BOTL, Swindon. The Lamborghini was purchased for £6,600 via dealer Nick Shrigley-Feigl of Knutsford Cheshire, at which time it was registered 'UCA 291V'. The Jarama remained with NS-F for several years, undergoing a repaint (colour change), bodywork repairs, retrim and new carpets in the early 1980s, these works adding a further circa £6,000 to the cost. The car was registered as 'VF 25' in 1982.In 1983 the late owner returned from Saudi Arabia, where he had worked for the British Aircraft Corporation, and became a permanent UK resident. The car's regular maintenance was then entrusted to Ferdi's Garage of Lytham, Lancashire, whose bills for the period 1985 to 2019 are on file. A new clutch was fitted in 2005 at 67,000 kilometres, while the most recent invoice was for new tyres and wheel refurbishment by Modern Classics Ltd, Lytham in 2022 (£2,600). Also on file is an original sales brochure; a V5C Registration Certificate; and numerous old MoTs, one of which records an odometer reading of 55,000 kilometres in 1979. The car was last MoT'd in 2018 at 68,800 kilometres (the current reading is 69,016 kilometres). Please note the cherished registration number 'VF 25' is being retained and sold separately.

title: Ferrari 599 GTB Fiorano Coupé
provenance: Delivered new to a member of the Bahraini royal family, only three owners from new.
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 2007

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Six-speed manual transmission•	Delivered new a member of the Bahraini royal family•	Only three owners from new•	Special one-off carbon-fibre rear diffuser•	Circa 35,000 kilometres (21,750 miles) from new•	UK taxes paid"The Ferrari 599 offers mind-blowing pace and handling. Quite possibly the best Ferrari of its generation. We'll spare the 911 Turbo the ignominy of comparison times, because the Ferrari has moved the game onto another level." – Autocar. Introduced at the Geneva Motor Show in February 2006, the 599 GTB Fiorano took its name from Ferrari's famous test track and was the latest in a succession of models named after places associated with the marque such as Modena and Maranello. In designing the 599, Ferrari abandoned the tubular steel chassis of the 550/575, adopting a more advanced and lighter all-aluminium chassis of greatly increased stiffness. Styled by Pininfarina under the direction of Ferrari's Frank Stephenson, the 599 with its long bonnet, small cabin, raised haunches and aggressive stance seemed the very definition of the term 'sports car'. The body's aerodynamics were developed in the wind tunnel, where hours of testing ensured that the minimum of drag was combined with constant downforce regardless of set up, an important consideration in a 200mph road car. Styling details such as the front brake ducts and hot air outlets behind the front wheelarches recalled the great competizione Ferraris of the past while the tail incorporated Ferrari's characteristic twin circular lights. The heart of any Ferrari is its engine, and the 599's 48-valve, 6.0-litre V12 was a reworked version of that found in the Enzo supercar. As installed in the 599, this state-of-the-art unit produced a staggering 612bhp at 7,600rpm with maximum torque of 448lb/ft at 5,600 revs. Weighing a claimed 1,690kg, the 599 has a power-to-weight ratio of 362bhp per tonne, far eclipsing the 291bhp/tonne of its 575 Maranello predecessor. Developed as part of Ferrari's Formula 1 programme, the paddle shift gearbox had become a feature of its range-topping sports cars and was available in its latest form for the 599, capable of changing gear in a mere 100 milliseconds. A conventional six-speed gearbox was available also, although cars so equipped such as this one are exceedingly rare.Although active suspension had long been banned from Formula 1, its development for road cars had continued and the 599 came equipped with SCM magnetorheological 'semi-active' dampers. The latter's damping fluid changes in viscosity almost instantaneously when a magnetic field is applied, thereby altering the suspension characteristics. Damper controls were placed on the Formula 1-style steering wheel together with those for traction control and stability, as was the starter button. The 599's fortunate driver would find themself looking at a central analogue rev counter flanked by a similar speedometer and an electronic display screen for all other functions. Ferrari thoughtfully provided plentiful storage space within the sumptuous leather-trimmed interior. A rare manual transmission example, the fabulous and exclusive Ferrari supercar offered here was completed with a one-off carbon-fibre rear diffuser to the special order of Ferrari's then President, Luca Di Montezemolo, acting for the car's original owner, a member of the Bahraini royal family. The current owner purchased the 599 from the Ferrari dealer in Bahrain in 2012 and exported it to the UK in 2017 since when it has seen little use. Possessing excellent provenance, the car has covered a mere 35,000 kilometres (22,370 miles) from new. The service book shows regular servicing with stamps in 2007, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2013 and 2017 (at 34,890 kilometres). The current odometer reading is just over 35,000km. The Ferrari is not UK registered but comes with UK taxes paid.

title: Ferrari 330 GTC Coupé
provenance: Known ownership and service history from new; present ownership since January 1981.
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1968

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	One of only some 22 right-hand drive UK-delivered examples•	Well known in UK Ferrari circles•	Known ownership and service history from new•	Present ownership since January 1981•	Enthusiastically campaigned•	Offered fresh from a no-expense-spared professional restorationIntended to fill a gap in Ferrari's line-up between the four-seat 330 GT 2+2 and the racer-on-the-road 275 GTB, the two-seat 330 GTC debuted at the Geneva Motor Show in March 1966. Pininfarina's understated coachwork combined elements of the 275 GTS at the rear with touches of the 500 Superfast at the front, while beneath bonnet resided the 4.0-litre, 300bhp version of Ferrari's familiar, two-cam, 60-degree V12, as used in the 330 GT 2+2. The short (94.5" wheelbase) chassis followed Ferrari's established practice of tying together sturdy oval-section main tubes in a steel spaceframe, while the suspension was independent all round by wishbones and coil springs. First introduced on a road-going Ferrari (the 275 GTB) in 1964, the rear suspension incorporated the five-speed gearbox in a transaxle, an arrangement that created a better-balanced car.Much development work had concentrated on the reduction of noise levels in the cabin, which was luxuriously equipped in the best Gran Turismo manner: leather seats, electric windows and heated rear screen were standard; radio, air conditioning and Borrani wire wheels the options. With a top speed in excess of 150mph, excellent ride comfort and sure-footed handling, the 330 GTC could justifiably claim to be the finest of high-speed conveyances for two people and their luggage. Total production of the 330 GTC amounted to some 600 cars between 1966 and 1968, of which only some 22 were delivered to the UK in right-hand-drive form. Well known in UK Ferrari circles, this 330 GTC first entered John Gould's life in January 1981 when he saw it for sale at Maranello Concessionaires' Tower Hill Garage. John had been a keen Ferrari devotee since childhood when he had been smitten by the gorgeous looks of a 500 Superfast and 275 GTB, but this was the first occasion he had actually been in a position to afford one. Chassis number '11333' had been ordered on 26th March 1968 by the UK Ferrari importer, Maranello Concessionaires (order no. 363). The order form states: '330 GTC, right hand drive, Metallizzato Azzurro 1927 BM, Blue VM 3015, Alloys.' On 30th July 1968 '11333' was despatched from Italy by air to London Heathrow against factory invoice no. 1537/68. Maranello Concessionaires supplied the car to Rob Walker Corsley Garage Ltd, Warminster on 5th August 1968, and two days later it was sold to first owner G J Rennison of Wolverhampton. The Ferrari was registered 'MMR 97G'.On 23rd September 1969 the car was sold to R A Cookson of Wylam, Northumberland via Maranello Concessionaires and registered 'RAC 46'. The registration changed to 'VTN 268G' on 23rd October 1980. John Gould bought the Ferrari from Maranello Concessionaires on 23rd January 1981 at 44,562 miles (bill of sale on file). John's work abroad meant that opportunities to enjoy the Ferrari were few and far between at first, and he did not get to use it regularly until his final return home circa 1990. Since then it has been enthusiastically campaigned, attending various Ferrari Owners Club concours events and Ferrari Days at Spa Francorchamps more than once, and appearing on the Ferrari Owners Club stand at the NEC Classic Car Show in both 2004 and 2005. John's 330 GTC also won the FOC's Ladies' Cup in 2005 and Yorkshire Ferrari's John Ashworth Memorial Trophy in 2006. Written for the Ferrari Owners Club magazine, a copy of John's account of his ownership is on file. Remarkably, '11333' also comes with a complete record of all servicing and maintenance works carried out from the time of the car's delivery in the UK up to November 2005 at 80,040 miles (inspection highly recommended). Notable developments along the way included a switch from the original Campagnolo alloy wheels to Borrani wires in 1991, and a respray by Kevin O'Rourke of Moto-Technique in 2003. Before John Gould died in 2019 the car had been placed with marque specialist Neal Lucas for a complete restoration. Prior to his passing John had expressed a wish that the restoration continue and it has only just been completed at a cost far in excess of £100,000. Works carried out include body repairs; chassis strip and refinish; engine strip and rebuild; suspension and braking systems overhaul; full repaint; full re-chrome; new carpets; and new tyres. The car will have been run-in prior to sale. Accompanying documentation is contained within three history files, and this impeccable Ferrari Gran Turismo also comes complete with its original wallet, handbook, parts catalogue, tool kit and spare keys. A unique opportunity. Sale proceeds to be donated to the charities Diabetes UK and The Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB).

title: Lamborghini Huracán LP 610-4 Coupé
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 2015

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	200mph supercar•	Circa 18,000 miles recorded•	Only one previous keeper•	Finance company repossession"While the Gallardo and Murciélago can be credited for revitalising Lamborghini for the 21st century, the Huracán felt like another big step into modernity when it arrived in 2014. On paper it ticked every box as a junior supercar to rival the likes of Ferrari's 458 and the McLaren 650S: over 600bhp from Lambo's signature V10, four-wheel drive, a dual-clutch gearbox (finally) and a totally fresh design and interior." - evo magazine. The Huracán (Spanish for Hurricane) made its official debut at the 2014 Geneva Auto Show, with deliveries commencing later that year. Its chassis was an entirely new design in - mostly - aluminium, featuring a central tunnel and rear bulkhead in carbon fibre for increased stiffness. Powering the newcomer was a development of the 5.2-litre V10 shared with the outgoing Gallardo, which delivered its 610PS to the road via a seven-speed, dual clutch, electronically controlled, four-wheel drive transmission system. The compact coupé bodywork was typically Lamborghini, boasting its manufacturer's customary combination of smooth curves and sharp edges. This low-drag shape enabled the Huracán to breach the all-important 200mph benchmark, albeit by only two miles per hour, with the 0-97km/h (0-60mph) dash accomplished in a mere 2.5 seconds. Braking was handled by carbon discs all round. The interior was notable as the first use by Lamborghini of parent-company Audi's 12.3" TFT 'virtual cockpit', and featured the customary heated/adjustable seating and leather/Alcantara upholstery. Other notable features include full LED headlamps, power steering, and an ANIMA (Adaptive Network Intelligent Management) driving modes selector controlling the engine, transmission, suspension, brakes, etc. The Huracán also met the demanding EU6 emissions targets. First registered on 23rd June 2015, this Huracán has had only one previous keeper (from date of registration to 11th December 2015) and is offered for sale as a finance company repossession. Accompanying documentation consists only of an HPI check report printout (the V5C will follow post-sale).

title: Ferrari 458 Italia Coupé
provenance: Formerly part of a large private collection in Hong Kong
description_block:

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Formerly part of a large private collection in Hong Kong•	Purchased and brought to the UK by the vendors•	Recently resprayed (all bills and 'before' photographs available)•	All books and tools"Back in 2009 the Ferrari 458 Italia emerged from the famous factory gates in Maranello to replace the 430. Its ancestry reaches all the way back to the late '60s Dino, the car named after Enzo Ferrari's son that forged the concept of the 'junior Ferrari' and introduced the mid-engined platform to the brand." – evo magazine.Although officially announced as the F430's successor, the 458 was an entirely new design, incorporating technologies developed as part of the Italian manufacturer's Formula 1 programme. The 458's specification and performance suggested that it was anything but a 'junior' Ferrari, as it boasted a 4.5-litre V8 engine producing 562bhp, an output good enough for a top speed of 325km/h (202mph). Reflecting the ongoing trend among supercars towards clutch-less semi-automatic transmissions, a seven-speed Getrag gearbox of that type was the only one available on the 458. To the regret of many enthusiasts, Ferrari's classic gated manual 'box was no longer an option. In keeping with Ferrari tradition, the 458's body was designed by Carrozzeria Pininfarina under the supervision of Ferrari's design director, Donato Coco. As one would expect of a car with a 200mph-plus capability, aerodynamics played a major role in the design, yet despite generating considerable downforce the 458's beautifully curvaceous body was remarkably devoid of extraneous appendages. Former Ferrari Formula 1 driver Michael Schumacher had a hand in the design of the interior, which featured a steering wheel incorporating many of the controls normally located on the dashboard or on stalks, as found in modern competition cars.   Despite the apparent handicaps of 135kg weight disadvantage and regular road tyres, the 458 lapped Ferrari's Fiorano test circuit quicker than the track-focused 430 Scuderia. "This was the result of Ferrari going for gold in every department," declared evo. "The 458 represented a quantum leap in technological terms, bringing a hoard of new systems into play to create an enveloping, pure driving experience."Spin-off models were not long in coming, the first new 458 variant being the almost inevitable Spider, introduced in 2011. The Spider was followed in 2013 by the 458 Speciale, which offered even more performance than before. Revised bodywork and active aerodynamics were two of the many advances over the original 458, together with updated electronics and an engine that now produced 597bhp. In 2014 Ferrari introduced an open-top version: the 458 Speciale Aperta. Representing the model in its original coupé configuration, this right-hand drive Ferrari 458 Italia has come from a large private collection in Hong Kong where it was kept indoors together with its owner's 458 Spider, seeing minimal use. Purchased and brought to the UK by the vendors, the car had acquired some minor paintwork blemishes while in storage so was resprayed at a cost of circa £7,000 (see bills and 'before' photographs on file). Also on file are previous service invoices issued by the official dealer in Hong Kong together with some others issued since the car arrived in the UK. Offered complete with a V5C document, MoT to July 2026, and all books and tools, this beautiful modern Ferrari is presented in impressive condition throughout.

title: Ferrari 328 GTS Targa Coupé
provenance: Delivered new to Josef Rotschne through the Austrian Ferrari dealer Wolfgang Denzel in January 1989
description_block:
YEAR_MANUFACTURED: 1989

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	Incredibly original 'time warp' condition•	Left-hand drive•	Classic colour combination•	Serviced by Carrs of ExeterIntroduced in 1985, the Ferrari 328 GTB/GTS was similar to the preceding 308 version apart from its 3.2-litre engine. Representing the second generation of Ferrari's V8-engined road cars, the entirely new 308 GTB had debuted at the Paris Salon in 1975. This particular model line had begun in 1973 with the Dino-badged 308 GT4 2+2, which took over from the preceding V6-engined Dino 246 GT. The newcomer's wedge-shaped styling - by Bertone rather than the customary Pininfarina - was not universally well received but the performance of the amidships-mounted, double-overhead-camshaft 3.0-litre V8 certainly was, and a dry-sump version of the same power unit was used for the 308 GT4's two-seat successor. Built on a shorter wheelbase, the stunningly beautiful 308 GTB marked a welcome return to Pininfarina styling. Further developments included the introduction in 1977 of an open-top GTS version with Targa-style removable roof, the adoption of Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection (1980) and, finally, revised cylinder heads with four valves per cylinder (1982). The 308 was superseded by the mechanically similar but larger engined 328 GTB in 1985. By increasing both bore and stroke, the quattrovalvole engine's capacity was raised to 3,186cc which, together with a higher compression ratio, revised pistons and an improved Marelli engine management system, lifted maximum power to 270bhp. Top speed was raised to within a whisker of 160mph (258km/h) with the sprint to 100km/h covered in a fraction over 5.5 seconds. On the outside, the elegant simplicity of Pininfarina's original 308 had been diluted somewhat by the addition of Testarossa-style moulded bumpers incorporating both sidelights and indicators, deeper rear valance and an unobtrusive roof spoiler. Its underlying beauty though, could not be disguised. "In our book, this is still the most beautiful of all contemporary exotics - a gorgeous looking car," declared Motor magazine.This 328 GTS was delivered new to Josef Rotschne through the Austrian Ferrari dealer Wolfgang Denzel in January 1989 and shows 49 kilometres on the odometer. The car presents beautifully, whether viewed from the front, rear, above or underneath. The expected signs of ageing bodywork are absent, and the shut lines and panel gaps are crisp and consistent throughout. Even the black plastic elements on the rear spoiler, wing mirrors, and engine and side window louvres have resisted cracking. Likewise, the black finish on the removable Targa roof, which is a snug fit. The Rosso Corsa paintwork presents well, while the Crema leather interior matches the exterior in terms of originality, authenticity and condition; even the instructions label for the Veglia Borletti quartz clock is still in place. Opening the boot reveals a similarly well-presented space containing a full-size spare wheel and a Ferrari tool roll. Having covered a mere 49 kilometres in 36 years, this car does not come with a great deal of history; nevertheless. In 2019, the Ferrari had its '2nd year' annual service with main dealer Carrs of Exeter. The service included the replacement of all cam belts, auxiliary belts and tensioners, plus a new battery and replacement bonnet and boot struts. Carrs also carried out some maintenance work and fitted new gaskets and seals to the gearbox and sump in October 2023. The car comes with a book pack and keys, but there is no registration document present. A unique opportunity.

title: De Tomaso Mangusta Coupé
description_block:

DESCRIPTION_BLOCK: •	One of an estimated circa 250 surviving out of 401 made•	Rare right-hand drive example•	Present ownership since 1996•	Regularly serviced, MoT'd and maintainedOne of the very first supercars, the Mangusta effectively established De Tomaso as a serious automobile manufacturer on its arrival in 1967. The Mangusta (mongoose) was powered by a mid-mounted 289ci (4.7-litre) Ford V8 engine. Also used to power Ford's GT40 Le Mans challenger, the iconic '289' produced 306bhp as installed in the Mangusta, which also used the GT40's early-type ZF transaxle. Later Mangusta production used the Ford 302ci (5.0-litre) engine together with a ZF transmission. Carrozzeria Ghia's Giorgetto Giugiaro contributed the striking coachwork featuring 'gull wing' engine covers, which had been intended for Giotto Bizzarrini. With 300-or-so horsepower on tap in its original form, the aerodynamic Mangusta was good for a top speed in the region of 155mph. All-round disc brakes helped restrain this outstanding performance. Alejandro De Tomaso enjoyed close links with the Ford Motor Company at this time and the American firm helped put the Mangusta into larger scale production than would otherwise have been possible. Nevertheless, only 401 examples were made between 1967 and 1972 compared with 765 examples of the contemporary Lamborghini Miura, and any Mangusta is extremely rare. The three marque registries estimate that there are only some 250 Mangustas remaining worldwide, making these survivors very rare and all the more so in right-hand drive form, as seen here. This Mangusta was first registered on 26th January 1972 and according to the old-style buff logbook was previous registered as 'JLB 9K' and 'TES 64'. The first keeper was a Michael P D StJ Neilan of London W1, who was followed by Sidney Foreman of London NW9 (1974) and then John Webster of Bradford, Yorkshire (1975). According to a previous owner, this car has appeared in a few publications/books by Richard Nichols and in the gentleman's magazine, Mayfair!The late owner acquired the Mangusta in 1996 when it was registered 'ABW 84K'; its previous keeper was Michael Parsley of Southampton (1990) and the deal was done directly for the sum of £27,000. The recorded mileage in 1990 was 22,546 and in 2020 it was 28,773. Since 1997 the car has been regularly serviced, MoT'd and maintained by Ferdi's Garage in Lytham, Lancashire. There is a bill on file for £4,600 for a new exhaust and front wheel bearings in 2010. Ferdi's last bill was issued in 2020. The history file also contains an owner's handbook, and original brochure and a V5C document.
