title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch plywood cabinet from the Grateful Dead’s “Wall of Sound” speaker system for Keith Godchaux’s acoustic piano. The cabinet features a pair of JBL D120F loudspeakers—high efficiency, 12 in. Alnico drivers codeveloped by JBL and Fender.   This cabinet was built in early 1974 by Alembic workers in conjunction with the Grateful Dead road crew—later known as Hard Truckers—in the San Francisco Bay Area. The materials, joinery, custom brackets, and removable baffle match other documented Wall of Sound boxes. It was numbered “208” and stenciled “PIANO,” marking it as part of Keith’s array.   Back of frame carries “G.D.” (Grateful Dead), “Ram…,” (Referring to the band’s roadie Laurence Shurtliff aka “Ramrod.” “Lumier,” “S.F.,” referring to the Lumiere Theatre and the date “32374,” the day the completed Wall of Sound debuted at the Cow Palace in Daly City, California.  On 23 March 1974, the fully realized “Wall of Sound” made its touring debut at the Cow Palace. The “32374” marking on one of the D120F frames aligns with that rollout. The piano cabinets—including No. 208—were used behind and above the band as part of the modular piano array, giving Keith Godchaux his channel. When the system was adapted for the European leg later that year, piano and bass cabinets like this one were part of the traveling inventory.

title: The Beatles
description_block: This 10 ½ in. EMI master tape is an effects tape that was used during the overdubbing and mixing stages of the album. It contains nearly 22 minutes of takes/tracks of songs written by John Lennon and recorded toward the end of the recording process. Included on the tape are the following recordings:  1. Recorded 8 October 1968 – An unreleased take of “I’m So Tired,” focusing on John’s vocals. Includes Lennon’s count in (1-2-3) and a single tracked (not double, like the release) alternate take with Lennon’s vocal in front. Ringo’s drums are way in the background with Mellotron keyboard and no rhythm guitar. Includes four full takes and four with tape roll-back.  2. Recorded 8 October 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “I’m So Tired” – Includes unused George Harrison guitar solo “track” meant for “I’m So Tired” and never released. This solo lays on top of the Mellotron and Ringo’s drums. This can be heard faintly on a version of “I’m So Tired” in the 50th Anniversary box set; the entire backing track in full studio quality included herein.  3. Recorded 25 September 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “Happiness is a Warm Gun” – This unused backing track includes Mellotron, Ringo Starr’s drums, and George Harrison guitar solos, piano, and tambourine. Includes one full take and two with tape roll back.  4. Recorded 29 August 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “Dear Prudence” – This unused backing track includes the backing harmonies (“aaaah, ooohs”) and hand clapping. Lennon’s vocals can be heard in the background.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch plywood cabinet with JBL K120 and JBL 2202A loudspeakers, built specifically for keyboardist Keith Godchaux’s piano channel and engineered to capture the instantaneous, vertical hammerstrike of a grand piano. Cabinet was built in early 1974 by members of the Grateful Dead road crew—known in later years as Hard Truckers—in collaboration with the Alembic shop in San Francisco.   During the 1974 Wall of Sound tour in the United States, the cabinet was part of the dedicated piano cluster feeding Keith Godchaux’s grand piano. When the system was scaled and adapted for European dates later that year, piano and bass cabinets like this one traveled with the band.  “209” handwritten in marker on the back and right side, consistent with Wall of Sound box numbering practices. “PIANO” hand-stenciled in blue paint on the back toward the bottom (partially over sprayed with white paint), identifying this box as part of the piano array. On the JBL K120, the interior paper cone bears the signature “Kevin Konecky” in white marker. Konecky was a Wall of Sound audio engineer who worked closely with Owsley “Bear” Stanley on design, setup, and nightly operation. On the interior frame of the JBL 2202A, the name “Stereo Doctor” is written in white marker, echoing the nickname used for Owsley “Bear” Stanley in his capacity as the system’s chief sound architect. A period “Grim Reaper” violinist sticker appears on the right side of the cabinet. This image, designed by Alton Kelley, was used on Grateful Dead tour stickers circa 1973 and is frequently associated with the Dead’s own stage and road gear from that era.  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker: 21 x 16 ½ x 26 in.  Road case: 25 ½ x 19 ¾ x 29 ½ in.

title: Neil Young
description_block: 3pcs. Lyrics and chord notations in blue ballpoint pen and pencil, written by Neil Young with additional words written by unknown person. All chord notations by Neil Young throughout. 2 pcs. measuring 7 ⅞ x 10 in.; 1 pc. measuring 5 x 8 in. Pages in good condition, with some yellowing from age and storage.    “I Wonder” lyrics and chords written by Young on recto of smaller page, with song entitled “All My Loving” on verso, written by Young. Other two pages, containing a combination of lyrics and chord notations for “All My Loving,” “Cleopatra” and “I Wonder” are blank on verso. Song titles in red marker written by unknown person.

title: Bob Dylan
description_block: 12 x 12 in.   (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) album, inscribed “London Rocks!!” and signed on the front cover by Bob Dylan, Rupert Everett, and Fiona (Flanagan) in silver marker.

title: The Sugarhill Gang
description_block: 13 ¼ x 15 in. Test pressing of the Sugarhill Gang’s “Rapper’s Delight,” slabbed and rated A for “authentic” by Audio Media Grading. The center label, handwritten by Master Gee in red ink, reads “Rapper’s Delight / 33 [RPM] / Sugar Hill Gang.” Record itself measures 12”. This record is exceedingly rare—fewer than 10 known test pressings of “Rapper’s Delight” are known to exist.

title: The Jimi Hendrix Experience
description_block: 8 ¼ x 11 ¾ in. (8 ¼ x 5 ⅞ in. folded). Handbill from the Jaguar Club in Herford, Germany, signed on verso by the Jimi Hendrix Experience—Jimi Hendrix, Noel Redding, and Mitch Mitchell—in conjunction with their performance at the club on 28 May 1967. Typed and annotated schedule on recto. Also features hand-drawn black and pink illustration of Jimi Hendrix’s name in psychedelic style on verso, next to signatures. Handbill has been folded, with visible horizontal and vertical crease lines.

title: The Rolling Stones
description_block: 7 in. Rolling Stones acetate with "Apple Corps Ltd." label and song title “Angie,” handwritten in blue ink and B-side “Silver Train;” Released in August 1973, hit single "Angie" appeared on the band's   album. There is no label on the “Silver Train” side of the acetate.  The disc exhibits light surface scratches; overall very good condition. Green and white label is slightly discolored. The sound quality of the recording on the disc is excellent with a slightly brighter mix, vibrant highs and strong bass, having been dubbed directly from the master tape recording.

title: Eric Clapton
description_block: A pre-production prototype of the Eric Clapton EC Fender Stratocaster, serial #V037766, with pewter finish and Fender Lace Sensor Pickups as per Clapton’s specifications.     Letter from Lee Dickson, Eric Clapton’s guitar tech from 1979-2009, states that “the instrument is a pre-production prototype Eric Clapton model in Pewter that was supplied by the Fender Custom Shop and features an early heavy v neck profile….guitar was played and used by Eric Clapton prior to the release of the official Fender production Eric Clapton signature model.”    Offered with Fender case and signed letter of authenticity from Lee Dickson.      Guitar: 39 x 12 ¾ x 2 in.   Case: 40 ½ x 14 x 5 in.

title: Neil Young
description_block: A Sunburst Les Paul Jr., serial # 614303, played by Neil Young on stage during his Continental Tour across North America and Europe. Offered with original Gibson case and signed letter of authenticity from Young’s longtime guitar tech Larry Cragg. Guitar: 39 x 13 x 2 in.  Case: 41 ½ x 15 x 4 ½ in.

title: Noel Gallagher | Oasis
description_block: An Epiphone EJ-200 acoustic guitar, serial # S94070027, previously owned and played by Noel Gallagher: principal songwriter and guitarist of the band Oasis. Guitar features fretboard inlays and Gibson’s decorative vine and flowers design on the pickguard. Lot includes letter of authenticity on Oasis and Creation Records letterhead signed by Noel Gallagher. Letter dated August 3, 1996, states “…guitar was used by Noel when he was writing songs for the album (What’s the Story Morning Glory) [sic].” Guitar is autographed by Noel Gallagher on the body, inscribed with a paint pen. Letter also states the guitar “can be seen in the “Wonderwall" promotional video.” Note: the official video for “Wonderwall” features numerous guitars similar in appearance to this EJ-200, and some which were covered with decorative craft paper that consequently obscured portions of the instruments.    Guitar in excellent condition, includes case and letter of authenticity signed by Gallagher. Guitar: 41 ¾ x 16 ¾ x 4 ⅝ in. Case: 43 x 18 x 5 ¾ in.

title: Syd Barrett | Pink Floyd
description_block: 2 manuscript pages measuring 8 x 13 in., 1 typed page measuring 8 x 10 in.  A collection of lyric sheets for Pink Floyd’s “Apples and Oranges,” the band’s third UK single and the final one written by Syd Barrett. Manuscript sheets written in blue ballpoint on off-white ruled notepaper. Typed page set in black on off-white copy paper. The typed page omits one line found in the first verse of the manuscript version: “Getting everything she wants from the supermarket stores.” Manuscript also includes three lines of accompanying guitar chords.

title: Joni Mitchell
description_block: 10 ⅝ x 14 in. 1 p. autograph manuscript lyrics for Joni Mitchell’s “Marcie,” from her 1968 debut album  . 23 lines, neatly written in sepia ink on cream paper, recto only.

title: The Rolling Stones
description_block: 8 ½ x 11 in. 14 pp. Souvenir program from the “All Stars ’64” UK tour presented by Robert Stigwood Associates Ltd., signed by the Rolling Stones in black pen on their individual artist page. Also signed throughout the program by other acts, including: Mike Berry, Billie Davis, The Le Roys, Don Spencer, and Billy Boyle. Light crease at bottom right.

title: Jimi Hendrix
description_block: 12 in. Trident Studios double-sided acetate for the stereo UK release of the Jimi Hendrix  album, released in June 1970. In very good condition, with some light marks to both sides of the acetate not affecting play.

title: Ravi Shankar
description_block: 29 booklets of Ravi Shankar’s score for the Concerto for Sitar and Orchestra—14 for Violin 1, 13 for Violin 2, one for Bass, and one for Horns 1 & 2—with annotations in pencil throughout, as well as four ragas handwritten in ballpoint: Marwa, Yaman, Nata [sic] Bhairav, and Bhimpalasi. Together with two invoice sheets on Tatra Corporation letterhead, one blank and one addressed to the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra.

title: Sex Pistols | The Clash
description_block: 19 ½ x 28 ⅞ in. Pink and black poster advertising the Sex Pistols’ 1976 “Anarchy in the UK” tour—with support from The Clash, The Damned, and other punk acts. Vintage condition consistent with age, storage, and identity. Tearing at bottom left, bottom center, and bottom right.

title: John Lennon | Yoko Ono
description_block: 8 x 7 ⅜ in. Paper memo from John Lennon and Yoko Ono, written by Lennon in black felt tip pen on Bag Productions letterhead. The memo reads: “When people want John/+/or/Yoko and they ask you – please refer them to our office – Diana – Sally – eg. John Peel – Tony Bramwell – C.B.S. – Jack Oliver – etc otherwise there is no fucking point in Bag Prod. – o.k. love John + Yoko”

title: Stevie Nicks
description_block: Black velvet jacket with dramatic collar, signed on synthetic lining by Stevie Nicks in silver ink. Label, no tags or closures. Seams loose/unattached at hem.  Jacket is 24 in. pit-to-pit, 16 in. shoulder-to-shoulder, 9 in. sleeve, 40 in. long, with 9 in. tall collar. Offered with certificate of authenticity from Funtyme Memorabilia.

title: Neil Young
description_block: The grey corduroy jacket, khaki pants and white dress shirt by Gentleman Farmer worn by Neil Young during the Continental tour. During the tour, Young commissioned painter Eric Johnson to create artwork live on stage during the shows. These paintings, produced during the concerts, often resulted in paint stains on Young’s clothing during his interaction with the artwork—clearly visible on the present suit. Blazer: 22 in. pit-to-pit, 32 ½ in. long, 25 ½ in. sleeve, 20 in. shoulder-to-shoulder Shirt: 24 in. pit-to-pit, 30 ¾ in. long, 25 ½ in. sleeve, 19 in. shoulder-to-shoulder Pants: 16 ½ in. waist, 32 in. inseam, 42 in. leg

title: Taylor Swift
description_block: 12 x 12 in.   album cover, signed by Taylor Swift in black marker.

title: Zephyr | Wild Style
description_block: 12 ½ x 10 ¼ in. 2 pp. Marker on paper, executed circa 1982, numbered “3a” in pencil at upper right corner. Artwork on one page reads “GRAFFITI,” with second page featuring shadowy outline in roughly the same shape.

title: Ed Sheeran
description_block: A Mitchell MD-100 acoustic guitar with mother of pearl decoration on sound hole, autographed by Ed Sheeran on body in black permanent marker. Inscription reads: “With love Ed Sheeran (Ed).” Together with gig bag.   Excellent condition; guitar has no strings and headstock has been repaired. Guitar: 42 x 16 x 4 ½ in. Case: 44 x 17 x 6 ½ in.

title: The Clash
description_block: Set of two 7” 45 RPM single records, both signed by the full band: Joe Strummer, Topper Headon, Mick Jones, and Paul Simonon. “White Riot” (B-side: “1977”) signed on cover in blue ballpoint. “(White Man) In Hammersmith Palais” (B-side: “The Prisoner”) signed on sleeve in black ballpoint.

title: Beastie Boys
description_block: 12 x 12 in.   album, signed on the front cover by Ad-Rock, Mike D, and MCA in black marker.

title: Stevie Nicks
description_block: A 9” tambourine played by Stevie Nicks live on stage and inscribed in black marker, “Much love Stevie Nicks enjoy!” Mounted in 21 ⅜ x 35 ¼ x 3 in. frame with a black and white photograph of Stevie Nicks signed in gold paint pen, “Much love Stevie Nicks.” Stevie Nicks plays tambourine when performing live and the instrument is an integral part of her stage persona.

title: George Harrison | Ravi Shankar
description_block: Two typescript letters belonging to Ravi Shankar: one from George Harrison, thanking Shankar for helping with the Concert for Bangladesh, stapled on top of another from UNICEF thanking both Harrison and Shankar for their significant support of and donation to the humanitarian agency. Typescript letters measure 8 ¼ x 10 ⅞ in. and 8 ½ x 11 in. respectively. Together with Shankar’s 5 ¾ x 4 ⅞ in. invitation to a June 1972 surprise party in honor of Harrison and Allen Klein’s distinguished service with regard to Bangladesh, in 6 x 5 in. envelope. Newspaper clipping from March 2021 featuring a retrospective article about the concert also included.

title: Bob Dylan
description_block: Dark metallic overshirt with silver stripes, custom-made for Bob Dylan. Synthetic material, with “Henry Duarte” label and no tags.  28 in. long, 22 in. pit-to-pit, 18 in. shoulder-to-shoulder, 20 in. sleeve. Offered with Letter of Provenance from designer Henry Duarte, featuring a photograph of Dylan wearing the overshirt.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This cabinet was built for the Grateful Dead’s 1974 Wall of Sound and originally housed a speaker that carried Phil Lesh’s bass or piano. In 1991, the cabinet was acquired by Simon Babbs, son of Ken Babbs who was a member of the Merry Pranksters and close collaborator of founder Ken Kesey. The cabinet was moved to the Kesey farm in Oregon where it was highly modified and painted red and white and then actively used by the Merry Pranksters Band. Photographs from early 1990s Fourth of July parties show the red Wall of Sound derived cabinets on the back of Kesey’s stage truck, with Ken and his wife Faye performing in front of them.  Cabinet has various stickers affixed including BOAC (British Airways) for air cargo for the 1974 European tour. Hand printed “PIANO” on back and “13.” “K140” signifying that cabinet originally contained a JBL K140 piano or bass speaker for Phil Lesh. “Parish” referring to the band’s stage manager Steve Parish. On the top of the cabinet is the handwritten notation “Property of Simon Babbs & Tom Bassett.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 19 ¼ x 16 ½ x 30 in.  Road case: 22 x 19 ¾ x 33 ½ in.

title: U2
description_block: 12 x 12 in. folded (24 x 12 in. unfolded).   vinyl insert signed by U2. Black-and-white landscape poster of the band on recto and lyrics on verso. Signed by Bono in blue felt tip pen, the Edge and Larry Mullen Jr. in black felt tip pen, and Adam Clayton in green felt tip pen. Good condition, with small crease at upper left corner and minor rippling visible on right side of verso.

title: Fleetwood Mac
description_block: 29 ¾ x 20 ¼ in. Original mechanical artwork for Fleetwood Mac’s iconic 1977 masterpiece,  . The artwork featuring black and white photographs by Herbert Worthington III. Design and layout by Desmond Strobel and calligraphy by Larry Vigon of Vigon Nahas Vigon. The mechanical artwork comprises two separate pieces of illustration board; each containing two photographs.   First illustration board comprises the front cover featuring Mick Fleetwood and Stevie Nicks striking the now iconic pose. Nicks in her supernatural “Rhiannon” persona. Mick Fleetwood wears black waistcoat, matching trousers, long stockings and ballet slippers. Fleetwood wearing his now infamous wooden balls with chains hanging from his waist that Fleetwood yanked out of a toilet tank years earlier and became his Talisman. Board also features back cover artwork with Worthington’s contact sheets and collage of various photographs, including outtakes from the session; conveying casualness and intimacy not typically used on album art. Overlay of onionskin paper with notes in red marker and black and blue ballpoint.   Second illustration board featuring gatefold artwork; two black and white photographs including outtakes from the session; comprising collage and contact prints by Worthington. With onion skin paper with notes in brown marker and black ballpoint, detailing retouching and printers instructions for Warner Brothers’ production department.

title: Led Zeppelin
description_block: 8 ½ x 5 ⅞ in. flyer, reinforced on cardstock, advertising Led Zeppelin’s shows at London’s Earl’s Court on 23, 24 and 25 May 1975. Signed in blue ballpoint by the band: Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones, and John Bonham. Excellent condition.

title: Stevie Ray Vaughn
description_block: An Electra 2249 “Super Rock” Japanese Les Paul-style guitar with blonde maple finish. Signed by Stevie Ray Vaughn on the body in black marker, underneath the clear pickguard.    39 x 13 x 2 ½ in.

title: Keith Moon | The Who
description_block: A group of Keith Moon-related ephemera: a pair of Olympic C drumsticks, stage-used by Moon; a 7” paper plate signed on recto by Moon in blue ink (exhibiting creases throughout and browning on verso); an original concert ticket for the Who’s 2 November 1973 show at King’s Hall, Belle Vue in Manchester (right corner torn); and a black coiled amp cable (with frayed end). Offered with letter of provenance from original owner, who obtained these items directly from the band during their aforementioned Manchester show.

title: Man Ray
description_block: Man Ray 1890 - 1976 signed  and dated  (lower right) charcoal and  on paper 14 ⅞ by 11 in. 37.8 by 27.9 cm.  Executed in New York in 1912. Andrew Strauss and Timothy Baum of the Man Ray Expertise Committee have confirmed the authenticity of this work under reference 00292-D-2023 and that it will be included in the Catalogue of Works on Paper of Man Ray, currently in preparation.

title: Ivan Puni (Jean Pougny)
description_block: Property from a Private Collection, New York Ivan Puni (Jean Pougny) 1890 - 1956 signed  (lower right) oil on canvas 9 ⅜ by 12 ⅞ in.  23.8 by 32.7 cm. Executed in 1929.

title: Bernard Buffet
description_block: Property from a Private Collection Bernard Buffet 1928 - 1999 signed   and dated  (upper left) oil on canvas  35 ⅛ by 51 in.  89.2 by 130 cm.  Executed in 1961. This artwork is listed in the archives of the Maurice Garnier Gallery. A certificate of authenticity has previously been issued for this piece, but it is currently lost. No duplicate certificate or any other documentation will be issued.

title: Mary Bradish Titcomb
description_block: Beyond the Brushstroke: The Sam & Marilyn Fox Collection Mary Bradish Titcomb 1858 - 1927 signed   (lower right) oil on canvas laid down on board 25 ⅛ by 30 in. 63.8 by 76.2 cm.

title: Tupac Shakur
description_block: 8 x 10 ½ in. 2pp. Letter on lined ruled paper with three-hole punch; handwritten and inscribed by Tupac in blue ballpoint with envelope postmarked 5 July 1995; return address lists Clinton Correctional Facility in Dannemora, New York, where Tupac Shakur was serving time for sexual assault. Envelope and letter exhibit some folding and staining.  The letter states: “I’m sure by now you know I got set up by Stretch and some Brooklyn n***** 2 take this rape charge then when I caught on they tried 2 kill me but u know I'm hard 2 kill so I'm still here ... I thought Stretch was my man but when the shit got hot he dissed me & let me get shot up!"  Signed “4 Life / 2PAC / HARD 2 KILL.”  Randy "Stretch" Walker was Tupac's best friend, and was with Tupac during the shooting at Quad Studios on 30 November 1994. Signatures include: Jimmy Page, Neil Young, Bob Dylan, Run D.M.C., Eric Clapton, Black Sabbath, Madonna, Tom Petty, The Rolling Stones, Led Zeppelin, Bette Midler, and George Segal. description_block: White casual dress shirt with deep-V neckline and front pocket, worn by George Michael during a performance of “Careless Whisper” on BBC television program   in 1984. Manufactured by Victor Shirts, Ibiza.  23 ½ in. pit-to-pit. 33 in. long.

description_block: 8 x 12 ⅞ in. Red pencil illustration of two male caricatures, drawn on the reverse of a typed list of welfare, nursery, and health centers in Liverpool.  Pinholes along left edge; small tears along right edge. Drawings intact.

title: George Harrison | Ravi Shankar
description_block: Two typescript letters belonging to Ravi Shankar: one from George Harrison, thanking Shankar for helping with the Concert for Bangladesh, stapled on top of another from UNICEF thanking both Harrison and Shankar for their significant support of and donation to the humanitarian agency. Newspaper clipping from March 2021 featuring a retrospective article about the concert also included.

title: Sex Pistols | The Clash
description_block: 19 ½ x 28 ⅞ in. Pink and black poster advertising the Sex Pistols’ 1976 “Anarchy in the UK” tour—with support from The Clash, The Damned, and other punk acts. Vintage condition consistent with age, storage, and identity. Tearing at bottom left, bottom center, and bottom right.

title: Taylor Swift
description_block: 12 x 12 in.   album cover, signed by Taylor Swift in black marker.

title: Bruce Springsteen
description_block: 8 ⅜ x 11 in. 1p. Manuscript, written by Bruce Springsteen in pencil on lined notebook paper. features developmental draft of “Backstreets,” with several lines from the finished work, including: “Just another tramp of hearts crying tears of faithlessness…. Stranded in the park and forced to confess.”    Released on Bruce Springsteen's 1975 masterwork,  , “Backstreets” is evocative of Bob Dylan’s “Positively 4th Street,” particularly in the melody and organ, which bear a strong resemblance to the Dylan song.

title: Freddie Mercury
description_block: This burgundy red Fender Telecaster, serial #S835696, was owned and played by Queen’s lead vocalist and songwriter Freddie Mercury. Guitar shows wear from moderate use.    Mercury gave the present guitar to his close friend Paul Prenter. Letter from Paul Prenter states: “He [Freddie Mercury] had it at home and played it but said that I should have it.”      Guitar: 38 ½ x 12 ½ x 1 ⅞ in.  Case: 40 ½ x 18 ½ x 5 in.    Offered with case and letter from Paul Prenter.

title: Bob Dylan
description_block: A Martin Smith W-101-N-PK acoustic guitar, autographed on body by Bob Dylan in black marker, Joan Baez in silver marker, Eric Andersen in red marker, and Charlie Sexton in silver marker. Dylan has added “Best wishes;” Baez has added “Sending Love;” Andersen has added “5/13/22 / Italy” to mark the date of his corresponding Bob Dylan tribute concert in Parma on that day. title: The Clash
description_block: Set of two 7” 45 RPM single records, both signed by the full band: Joe Strummer, Topper Headon, Mick Jones, and Paul Simonon. “White Riot” (B-side: “1977”) signed on cover in blue ballpoint. “(White Man) In Hammersmith Palais” (B-side: “The Prisoner”) signed on sleeve in black ballpoint.

title: Noel Gallagher | Oasis
description_block: A 12-string Rickenbacker 360 with Fireglow finish, owned and played by Oasis’ principal songwriter and lead guitarist Noel Gallagher for over ten years of the band’s history. Autographed by Noel Gallagher on the pickguard, “God bless – Noel Gallagher.”  Letter of provenance from Oasis’ guitar tech Jason Rhodes states: "this was the only Rickenbacker Fireglow 12 String the band owned and so any studio pictures out there featuring a 12 string Ricky it is definitely this guitar.”  Offered with signed letter from Oasis guitar tech Jason Rhodes, photograph of Gallagher signing the instrument, and original metal flight case featuring “Oasis” stenciled in white.  Guitar: 39 ¼ x 15 x 2 ½ in. Case: 46 ¼ x 19 ⅜ x 5 ¾ in.

title: Jimi Hendrix
description_block: 7 ⅛ x 7 in. Sleeve for Jimi Hendrix’s “Purple Haze,” signed by Hendrix on recto in black marker. Small piece of black tape affixed around top left corner of recto. Sleeve exhibits cracking along edges and slightly bumped corners. Signature and album artwork intact on both sides.

title: The Beatles
description_block: 23 ½ x 18 ¾ in. Replica of the 1967 Ludwig bass drum with Ringo Starr’s classic black pearl finish and a recreation of the iconic Beatles Drop-T logo on the drumskin. In excellent condition.   Offered with heavy duty case and letter of authenticity from Phil Harris of Harris Hire, who sourced the drum for the video, as well as accompanying photos and a still from the video.

title: Bill Wyman
description_block: A Fender Musicmaster short scale bass guitar, serial #328371, originally belonging to Rolling Stones bassist Bill Wyman. Features cream finish and white Pearloid pickguard. Light play wear. Together with original hard case.      Guitar: 42 x 12 x 2 in.   Case: 44 ½ x 14 ½ x 4 in.

title: Little Richard | Bo Diddley
description_block: 22 x 28 ⅜ in. Three-color concert poster printed by The Globe Poster Co., advertising the “Top Ten Rhythm & Blues Review” on 27 September 1955 at the Memorial Auditorium in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Lineup includes Bo Diddley, Big Joe Turner, The Clovers, and others.    Together with 22 x 28 ¼ in. four-color concert poster printed by The Globe Poster Co., advertising the “Top Ten Review of 1956” on 5 November 1956 at Memorial Auditorium in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Lineup includes Little Richard, Big Joe Turner, Etta James, The Moonglows and others.   Both in very good condition, with some yellowing at edges due to age and storage.

title: John Lennon
description_block: 5 pcs. Comprising the following: A 9 ½ x 11 ½ in. book with pebbled black cover. A printed copy of Lennon’s original, with hand-drawn illustrations to help him recall his learning, bound and gifted by Lennon to his Japanese instructor, Tamiko Steinberg. Features 94 original drawings throughout; Lennon has penned an added inscription to “Steinberg san,” with a doodle of a sheep saying “Domo arigato!” in ballpoint on the inside front cover; A 5 ¼ x 8 ¼ in. blue Berlitz course workbook, throughout which Lennon has added dozens of notes and humorous doodles in pencil;  A 5 ⅞ x 3 ⅞ in. postcard, addressed to "Steinberg san" and signed by Lennon, who has added his signature family portrait of him, Sean and Yoko, with “People compliment me on my Japanese!” at bottom left, all in black ink; A collection of doodles in blue and black ink on 8 ½ x 2 ¾ in. ruled paper; A drawing with the caption, “Experts are boomerang rounding the world” in black ink on 8 x 5 in. unlined paper.  Wear consistent with age and storage.

title: Stevie Nicks
description_block: A black felt top hat with red fabric band and silver encrusted moon-and-star brooch, signed by Stevie Nicks in gold ink. The hat is 6 ¼ in. tall, with a 21 ½ in. circumference and a 2 ¼ in. brim. Offered with JSA Letter of Authenticity.

title: The Rolling Stones
description_block: 7 in. Rolling Stones acetate with "Apple Corps Ltd." label and song title “Angie,” handwritten in blue ink and B-side “Silver Train;” Released in August 1973, hit single "Angie" appeared on the band's   album. There is no label on the “Silver Train” side of the acetate.  The disc exhibits light surface scratches; overall very good condition. Green and white label is slightly discolored. The sound quality of the recording on the disc is excellent with a slightly brighter mix, vibrant highs and strong bass, having been dubbed directly from the master tape recording.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch-plywood speaker cabinet prototype was built in June 1972 at the Alembic shop by Rick Turner and Ron Wickersham labeled “COSMIC 672” in red; similar to other Alembic PA cabinets built for the Dead in 1972 and 1973. Cabinet also contained a JBL K140 Speaker for the piano that was converted into a bass cabinet for Phil Lesh with handprinted “Parish Side.” Steve Parish was stage manager for the 1974 Grateful Dead and a member of the band’s road crew.   This cabinet is one of Stanley “Bear’” Owsley’s first hifi creations that had individual Altec and JBL speakers for each instrument, driven by McIntosh power amps—and that debuted at the Cow Palace on March 23, 1974.  In practice, cabinets such as the “COSMIC 672” were the pieces the crew listened to, measured, and retuned as they worked out how to eliminate distortion, remove the need for stage monitors, and give each player a dedicated, full range PA of their own.  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 30 ¾ x 15 x 14 ¾ in.  Road case: 34 ½ x 18 ½ x 16 ¼ in.

title: Freddie Mercury
description_block: Two-piece ivory seersucker suit, consisting of a double-breasted jacket and corresponding wide-leg pleated trousers.  Jacket: 22 in. pit-to-pit, 19 in. shoulder-to-shoulder, 19 ½ in. waist, 25 in. sleeve, 32 ½ in. long. Pants: 16 in. waist, 31 in. inseam, 43 ¾ in. long.

title: Freddie Mercury
description_block: 19 ½  x 19 ½ in. Poster from German teen magazine Popcorn, featuring Freddie Mercury in rainbow suspenders, a white shirt, and leather pants, singing into a microphone. Signed by Freddie in blue ink and inscribed “To Rüdiger.” Unsigned 1982 calendar featuring an image of Bucks Fizz on verso.

title: Queen
description_block: 3 ⅞ x 2 ⅞ in. Ticket stub for Queen’s 26 November 1975 concert at Free Trade Hall in Manchester, UK, signed in black ballpoint on recto by all four members of Queen: Freddie Mercury, Brian May, Roger Taylor, and John Deacon. Torn at bottom left corner; signatures intact.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This cabinet was built for the Grateful Dead’s 1974 “Wall of Sound” and originally housed a speaker that carried Phil Lesh’s bass or for piano. In 1991, the cabinet was acquired by Simon Babbs, son of Ken Babbs who was a member of the Merry Pranksters and close collaborator of founder Ken Kesey. The cabinet was moved to Ken Kesey’s farm in Oregon where it was highly modified and painted red and white and then actively used by the Merry Pranksters Band. Photographs from early 1990s Fourth of July parties show the red Wall of Sound derived cabinets on the back of Kesey’s stage truck, with Ken and his wife Faye performing in front of them.  Cabinet has various stickers affixed including a “Free the Hostages,” dating back to the Iran Hostage Crisis which took place from 1979 to 1981; “Hard Truckers” circular sticker from the 1970s and 1980s. On the top of the cabinet is the handwritten notation “Property of Simon Babbs & Tom Bassett.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 19 ¼ x 16 ½ x 30 in.  Road case: 22 x 19 ¾ x 33 ½ in.

title: Jimi Hendrix
description_block: 12 in. Trident Studios double-sided acetate for the stereo UK release of the Jimi Hendrix  album, released in June 1970. In very good condition, with some light marks to both sides of the acetate not affecting play.

title: Led Zeppelin
description_block: 8 ½ x 5 ⅞ in. flyer, reinforced on cardstock, advertising Led Zeppelin’s shows at London’s Earl’s Court on 23, 24 and 25 May 1975. Signed in blue ballpoint by the band: Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones, and John Bonham. Excellent condition.

title: Neil Young
description_block: 3 pcs. Manuscript on note paper and sheet music, handwritten by Neil Young. Features chord structure and lyrics for the song “Be My Girl” in blue ballpoint pen, with musical notation in pencil. All chord notations by Young. Other handwriting by unknown person.     “Be My Girl” is one of Young’s earliest ever written. Pages in very good condition, with some yellowing from age and storage. 1 pc. measuring 9 ¼ x 12 in.; 1 pc. measuring 5 x 8 in.; 1 pc. measuring 7 ⅞ x 10 in.

title: Pink Floyd
description_block: 21 ½ x 31 ½ in. Poster for The Pink Floyd’s “Games for May” concert event at Queen Elizabeth Hall in South London on 12 May 1967. Features blue and black artwork in a psychedelic style, designed by graphic artist Barry Zaid.

title: Chuck Berry
description_block: 22 ⅛ x 28 ¼ in. Four-color concert poster printed by The Globe Poster Co., advertising the “Big Rock & Roll Show” on 14 October 1955 at Memorial Auditorium in Chattooga, Tennessee. The multi-act show included the Chuck Berry Trio playing “Maybellene,” as well as Buddy Johnson, The Nutmegs, Arthur Prysock, The Spaniels, and others.   In excellent condition, with small tear to upper left corner.

title: Led Zeppelin
description_block: 4 ¾ x 4 ⅞ x 11 ¾ in. Led Zeppelin “The Object” obelisk-shaped statue made of gypsum cement. Featured in the artwork of Zeppelin’s 1976 album  and created as a promotional item in an edition of 1000; individually numbered. The present is #199/1000.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch plywood cabinet with JBL K120 and JBL 2202A loudspeakers, built specifically for keyboardist Keith Godchaux’s piano channel and engineered to capture the instantaneous, vertical hammerstrike of a grand piano. Cabinet was built in early 1974 by members of the Grateful Dead road crew—known in later years as Hard Truckers—in collaboration with the Alembic shop in San Francisco.   During the 1974 Wall of Sound tour in the United States, the cabinet was part of the dedicated piano cluster feeding Keith Godchaux’s grand piano. When the system was scaled and adapted for European dates later that year, piano and bass cabinets like this one traveled with the band.  “209” handwritten in marker on the back and right side, consistent with Wall of Sound box numbering practices. “PIANO” hand-stenciled in blue paint on the back toward the bottom (partially over sprayed with white paint), identifying this box as part of the piano array. On the JBL K120, the interior paper cone bears the signature “Kevin Konecky” in white marker. Konecky was a Wall of Sound audio engineer who worked closely with Owsley “Bear” Stanley on design, setup, and nightly operation. On the interior frame of the JBL 2202A, the name “Stereo Doctor” is written in white marker, echoing the nickname used for Owsley “Bear” Stanley in his capacity as the system’s chief sound architect. A period “Grim Reaper” violinist sticker appears on the right side of the cabinet. This image, designed by Alton Kelley, was used on Grateful Dead tour stickers circa 1973 and is frequently associated with the Dead’s own stage and road gear from that era.  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker: 21 x 16 ½ x 26 in.  Road case: 25 ½ x 19 ¾ x 29 ½ in.

title: The Beatles
description_block: This Selmer Truvoice Stadium amplifier (18 ¾” L x 10 ½” W x 21 ½” H) was used by The Beatles and other bands at the Star-Club in Hamburg, Germany, in 1962. The amp was donated to the Buddy Holly Educational Foundation by a family member who owned the Star-Club. Includes three vacuum tubes.   With letter of authenticity from Peter Bradley Jr. from the Buddy Holly Educational Foundation as well as photograph of Bradley with the amplifier.

title: Pete Townshend
description_block: A Takamine LTD-89 acoustic guitar, serial #89040666, owned and played by Pete Townshend of the Who. Guitar with spruce top, rosewood fingerboard and four channel EQ. Offered with hard case and letter of provenance from producer John Porter.    Letter from John Porter states that the guitar “was gifted by my good friend Alan Rogan, famed guitar technician to The Who, who confirmed that the instrument was owned and used by Pete Townshend of The Who.”      Guitar: 41 x 14 ¾ x 4 in.   Case: 45 x 19 x 7 ½ in.

title: Neil Young
description_block: The grey corduroy jacket, khaki pants and white dress shirt by Gentleman Farmer worn by Neil Young during the Continental tour. During the tour, Young commissioned painter Eric Johnson to create artwork live on stage during the shows. These paintings, produced during the concerts, often resulted in paint stains on Young’s clothing during his interaction with the artwork—clearly visible on the present suit. Blazer: 22 in. pit-to-pit, 32 ½ in. long, 25 ½ in. sleeve, 20 in. shoulder-to-shoulder Shirt: 24 in. pit-to-pit, 30 ¾ in. long, 25 ½ in. sleeve, 19 in. shoulder-to-shoulder Pants: 16 ½ in. waist, 32 in. inseam, 42 in. leg

title: The Rolling Stones
description_block: 12 x 12 in.   album, signed on the back cover by Keith Richards in blue marker.

title: Syd Barrett | Pink Floyd
description_block: 2 manuscript pages measuring 8 x 13 in., 1 typed page measuring 8 x 10 in.  A collection of lyric sheets for Pink Floyd’s “Apples and Oranges,” the band’s third UK single and the final one written by Syd Barrett. Manuscript sheets written in blue ballpoint on off-white ruled notepaper. Typed page set in black on off-white copy paper. The typed page omits one line found in the first verse of the manuscript version: “Getting everything she wants from the supermarket stores.” Manuscript also includes three lines of accompanying guitar chords.

title: Fleetwood Mac
description_block: 29 ¾ x 20 ¼ in. Original mechanical artwork for Fleetwood Mac’s iconic 1977 masterpiece,  . The artwork featuring black and white photographs by Herbert Worthington III. Design and layout by Desmond Strobel and calligraphy by Larry Vigon of Vigon Nahas Vigon. The mechanical artwork comprises two separate pieces of illustration board; each containing two photographs.   First illustration board comprises the front cover featuring Mick Fleetwood and Stevie Nicks striking the now iconic pose. Nicks in her supernatural “Rhiannon” persona. Mick Fleetwood wears black waistcoat, matching trousers, long stockings and ballet slippers. Fleetwood wearing his now infamous wooden balls with chains hanging from his waist that Fleetwood yanked out of a toilet tank years earlier and became his Talisman. Board also features back cover artwork with Worthington’s contact sheets and collage of various photographs, including outtakes from the session; conveying casualness and intimacy not typically used on album art. Overlay of onionskin paper with notes in red marker and black and blue ballpoint.   Second illustration board featuring gatefold artwork; two black and white photographs including outtakes from the session; comprising collage and contact prints by Worthington. With onion skin paper with notes in brown marker and black ballpoint, detailing retouching and printers instructions for Warner Brothers’ production department.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: Phil Lesh Bass Cabinet with JBL D140F Loudspeaker with birch construction built in the San Francisco Bay Area by the Grateful Dead road crew (later known as Hard Truckers) in collaboration with Alembic. Assigned to Phil Lesh's bass array and matched to his famous Osiris bass guitar. Lesh debuted his Osiris bass on stage 16 June 1974, and he played it at nearly every show through 1979, including footage shot at Cornell University on 8 May 1977, the Great Pyramid concerts, and the closing of Winterland. This cabinet was purpose-built for that specific instrument.  Lesh's bass setup featured a custom quadraphonic, six channel instrument that sent each of its four strings to a separate channel. This cabinet was one of the dedicated low frequency boxes in that bass array.  A New Riders of the Purple Sage sticker on the cabinet side places its use in 1974, when the New Riders regularly opened for the Dead and shared access to the “Wall of Sound.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 25 ¼ x 20 x 28 ½ in.   Road case: 29 x 23 ¾ x 32 ½ in.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch plywood cabinet from the Grateful Dead’s “Wall of Sound” speaker system for Keith Godchaux’s acoustic piano. The cabinet features a pair of JBL D120F loudspeakers—high efficiency, 12 in. Alnico drivers codeveloped by JBL and Fender.   This cabinet was built in early 1974 by Alembic workers in conjunction with the Grateful Dead road crew—later known as Hard Truckers—in the San Francisco Bay Area. The materials, joinery, custom brackets, and removable baffle match other documented Wall of Sound boxes. It was numbered “208” and stenciled “PIANO,” marking it as part of Keith’s array.   Back of frame carries “G.D.” (Grateful Dead), “Ram…,” (Referring to the band’s roadie Laurence Shurtliff aka “Ramrod.” “Lumier,” “S.F.,” referring to the Lumiere Theatre and the date “32374,” the day the completed Wall of Sound debuted at the Cow Palace in Daly City, California.  On 23 March 1974, the fully realized “Wall of Sound” made its touring debut at the Cow Palace. The “32374” marking on one of the D120F frames aligns with that rollout. The piano cabinets—including No. 208—were used behind and above the band as part of the modular piano array, giving Keith Godchaux his channel. When the system was adapted for the European leg later that year, piano and bass cabinets like this one were part of the traveling inventory.

title: The Beatles
description_block: This 10 ½ in. EMI master tape is an effects tape that was used during the overdubbing and mixing stages of the album. It contains nearly 22 minutes of takes/tracks of songs written by John Lennon and recorded toward the end of the recording process. Included on the tape are the following recordings:  1. Recorded 8 October 1968 – An unreleased take of “I’m So Tired,” focusing on John’s vocals. Includes Lennon’s count in (1-2-3) and a single tracked (not double, like the release) alternate take with Lennon’s vocal in front. Ringo’s drums are way in the background with Mellotron keyboard and no rhythm guitar. Includes four full takes and four with tape roll-back.  2. Recorded 8 October 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “I’m So Tired” – Includes unused George Harrison guitar solo “track” meant for “I’m So Tired” and never released. This solo lays on top of the Mellotron and Ringo’s drums. This can be heard faintly on a version of “I’m So Tired” in the 50th Anniversary box set; the entire backing track in full studio quality included herein.  3. Recorded 25 September 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “Happiness is a Warm Gun” – This unused backing track includes Mellotron, Ringo Starr’s drums, and George Harrison guitar solos, piano, and tambourine. Includes one full take and two with tape roll back.  4. Recorded 29 August 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “Dear Prudence” – This unused backing track includes the backing harmonies (“aaaah, ooohs”) and hand clapping. Lennon’s vocals can be heard in the background.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This cabinet was built for the Grateful Dead’s 1974 Wall of Sound and originally housed a speaker that carried Phil Lesh’s bass or piano. In 1991, the cabinet was acquired by Simon Babbs, son of Ken Babbs who was a member of the Merry Pranksters and close collaborator of founder Ken Kesey. The cabinet was moved to the Kesey farm in Oregon where it was highly modified and painted red and white and then actively used by the Merry Pranksters Band. Photographs from early 1990s Fourth of July parties show the red Wall of Sound derived cabinets on the back of Kesey’s stage truck, with Ken and his wife Faye performing in front of them.  Cabinet has various stickers affixed including BOAC (British Airways) for air cargo for the 1974 European tour. Hand printed “PIANO” on back and “13.” “K140” signifying that cabinet originally contained a JBL K140 piano or bass speaker for Phil Lesh. “Parish” referring to the band’s stage manager Steve Parish. On the top of the cabinet is the handwritten notation “Property of Simon Babbs & Tom Bassett.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 19 ¼ x 16 ½ x 30 in.  Road case: 22 x 19 ¾ x 33 ½ in.

description_block: Phil Lesh Bass Cabinet with JBL D140F Loudspeaker with birch construction built in the San Francisco Bay Area by the Grateful Dead road crew (later known as Hard Truckers) in collaboration with Alembic. Assigned to Phil Lesh's bass array and matched to his famous Osiris bass guitar. Lesh debuted his Osiris bass on stage 16 June 1974, and he played it at nearly every show through 1979, including footage shot at Cornell University on 8 May 1977, the Great Pyramid concerts, and the closing of Winterland. This cabinet was purpose-built for that specific instrument.  Lesh's bass setup featured a custom quadraphonic, six channel instrument that sent each of its four strings to a separate channel. This cabinet was one of the dedicated low frequency boxes in that bass array.  A New Riders of the Purple Sage sticker on the cabinet side places its use in 1974, when the New Riders regularly opened for the Dead and shared access to the “Wall of Sound.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 25 ¼ x 20 x 28 ½ in.   Road case: 29 x 23 ¾ x 32 ½ in.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch-plywood speaker cabinet prototype was built in June 1972 at the Alembic shop by Rick Turner and Ron Wickersham labeled “COSMIC 672” in red; similar to other Alembic PA cabinets built for the Dead in 1972 and 1973. Cabinet also contained a JBL K140 Speaker for the piano that was converted into a bass cabinet for Phil Lesh with handprinted “Parish Side.” Steve Parish was stage manager for the 1974 Grateful Dead and a member of the band’s road crew.   This cabinet is one of Stanley “Bear’” Owsley’s first hifi creations that had individual Altec and JBL speakers for each instrument, driven by McIntosh power amps—and that debuted at the Cow Palace on March 23, 1974.  In practice, cabinets such as the “COSMIC 672” were the pieces the crew listened to, measured, and retuned as they worked out how to eliminate distortion, remove the need for stage monitors, and give each player a dedicated, full range PA of their own.  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 30 ¾ x 15 x 14 ¾ in.  Road case: 34 ½ x 18 ½ x 16 ¼ in.

description_block: This cabinet was built for the Grateful Dead’s 1974 “Wall of Sound” and originally housed a speaker that carried Phil Lesh’s bass or for piano. In 1991, the cabinet was acquired by Simon Babbs, son of Ken Babbs who was a member of the Merry Pranksters and close collaborator of founder Ken Kesey. The cabinet was moved to Ken Kesey’s farm in Oregon where it was highly modified and painted red and white and then actively used by the Merry Pranksters Band. Photographs from early 1990s Fourth of July parties show the red Wall of Sound derived cabinets on the back of Kesey’s stage truck, with Ken and his wife Faye performing in front of them.  Cabinet has various stickers affixed including a “Free the Hostages,” dating back to the Iran Hostage Crisis which took place from 1979 to 1981; “Hard Truckers” circular sticker from the 1970s and 1980s. On the top of the cabinet is the handwritten notation “Property of Simon Babbs & Tom Bassett.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 19 ¼ x 16 ½ x 30 in.  Road case: 22 x 19 ¾ x 33 ½ in.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch plywood cabinet from the Grateful Dead’s “Wall of Sound” speaker system for Keith Godchaux’s acoustic piano. The cabinet features a pair of JBL D120F loudspeakers—high efficiency, 12 in. Alnico drivers codeveloped by JBL and Fender.   This cabinet was built in early 1974 by Alembic workers in conjunction with the Grateful Dead road crew—later known as Hard Truckers—in the San Francisco Bay Area. The materials, joinery, custom brackets, and removable baffle match other documented Wall of Sound boxes. It was numbered “208” and stenciled “PIANO,” marking it as part of Keith’s array.   Back of frame carries “G.D.” (Grateful Dead), “Ram…,” (Referring to the band’s roadie Laurence Shurtliff aka “Ramrod.” “Lumier,” “S.F.,” referring to the Lumiere Theatre and the date “32374,” the day the completed Wall of Sound debuted at the Cow Palace in Daly City, California.  On 23 March 1974, the fully realized “Wall of Sound” made its touring debut at the Cow Palace. The “32374” marking on one of the D120F frames aligns with that rollout. The piano cabinets—including No. 208—were used behind and above the band as part of the modular piano array, giving Keith Godchaux his channel. When the system was adapted for the European leg later that year, piano and bass cabinets like this one were part of the traveling inventory.

title: Zox | [Steely Dan]
description_block: 102 x 102 in. Acrylic on canvas artwork for Steely Dan’s fifth studio album,  , released in May 1976. The large-scale canvas depicts dramatic skyscrapers that are topped with menacing Gargoyle-type heads.  The final album cover was created from this painting and a photograph by Charlie Ganse depicting a man sleeping on a bench in public.  Condition consistent with age and storage, with foxing and some stains throughout. title: Bob Dylan

title: The Beatles
description_block: This 10 ½ in. EMI master tape is an effects tape that was used during the overdubbing and mixing stages of the album. It contains nearly 22 minutes of takes/tracks of songs written by John Lennon and recorded toward the end of the recording process. Included on the tape are the following recordings:  1. Recorded 8 October 1968 – An unreleased take of “I’m So Tired,” focusing on John’s vocals. Includes Lennon’s count in (1-2-3) and a single tracked (not double, like the release) alternate take with Lennon’s vocal in front. Ringo’s drums are way in the background with Mellotron keyboard and no rhythm guitar. Includes four full takes and four with tape roll-back.  2. Recorded 8 October 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “I’m So Tired” – Includes unused George Harrison guitar solo “track” meant for “I’m So Tired” and never released. This solo lays on top of the Mellotron and Ringo’s drums. This can be heard faintly on a version of “I’m So Tired” in the 50th Anniversary box set; the entire backing track in full studio quality included herein.  3. Recorded 25 September 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “Happiness is a Warm Gun” – This unused backing track includes Mellotron, Ringo Starr’s drums, and George Harrison guitar solos, piano, and tambourine. Includes one full take and two with tape roll back.  4. Recorded 29 August 1968 – Unreleased backing track for “Dear Prudence” – This unused backing track includes the backing harmonies (“aaaah, ooohs”) and hand clapping. Lennon’s vocals can be heard in the background.

title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This birch plywood cabinet with JBL K120 and JBL 2202A loudspeakers, built specifically for keyboardist Keith Godchaux’s piano channel and engineered to capture the instantaneous, vertical hammerstrike of a grand piano. Cabinet was built in early 1974 by members of the Grateful Dead road crew—known in later years as Hard Truckers—in collaboration with the Alembic shop in San Francisco.   During the 1974 Wall of Sound tour in the United States, the cabinet was part of the dedicated piano cluster feeding Keith Godchaux’s grand piano. When the system was scaled and adapted for European dates later that year, piano and bass cabinets like this one traveled with the band.  “209” handwritten in marker on the back and right side, consistent with Wall of Sound box numbering practices. “PIANO” hand-stenciled in blue paint on the back toward the bottom (partially over sprayed with white paint), identifying this box as part of the piano array. On the JBL K120, the interior paper cone bears the signature “Kevin Konecky” in white marker. Konecky was a Wall of Sound audio engineer who worked closely with Owsley “Bear” Stanley on design, setup, and nightly operation. On the interior frame of the JBL 2202A, the name “Stereo Doctor” is written in white marker, echoing the nickname used for Owsley “Bear” Stanley in his capacity as the system’s chief sound architect. A period “Grim Reaper” violinist sticker appears on the right side of the cabinet. This image, designed by Alton Kelley, was used on Grateful Dead tour stickers circa 1973 and is frequently associated with the Dead’s own stage and road gear from that era.  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker: 21 x 16 ½ x 26 in.  Road case: 25 ½ x 19 ¾ x 29 ½ in.

description_block: An Epiphone EJ-200 acoustic guitar, serial # S94070027, previously owned and played by Noel Gallagher: principal songwriter and guitarist of the band Oasis. Guitar features fretboard inlays and Gibson’s decorative vine and flowers design on the pickguard. Letter dated August 3, 1996, states “…guitar was used by Noel when he was writing songs for the album (What’s the Story Morning Glory) [sic].” Guitar is autographed by Noel Gallagher on the body, inscribed with a paint pen. Letter also states the guitar “can be seen in the “Wonderwall" promotional video.” Note: the official video for “Wonderwall” features numerous guitars similar in appearance to this EJ-200, and some which were covered with decorative craft paper that consequently obscured portions of the instruments.    Guitar in excellent condition, includes case and letter of authenticity signed by Gallagher. Manuscript sheets written in blue ballpoint on off-white ruled notepaper. Typed page set in black on off-white copy paper. title: Grateful Dead
description_block: This cabinet was built for the Grateful Dead’s 1974 Wall of Sound and originally housed a speaker that carried Phil Lesh’s bass or piano. In 1991, the cabinet was acquired by Simon Babbs, son of Ken Babbs who was a member of the Merry Pranksters and close collaborator of founder Ken Kesey. The cabinet was moved to the Kesey farm in Oregon where it was highly modified and painted red and white and then actively used by the Merry Pranksters Band. Photographs from early 1990s Fourth of July parties show the red Wall of Sound derived cabinets on the back of Kesey’s stage truck, with Ken and his wife Faye performing in front of them.  Cabinet has various stickers affixed including BOAC (British Airways) for air cargo for the 1974 European tour. Hand printed “PIANO” on back and “13.” “K140” signifying that cabinet originally contained a JBL K140 piano or bass speaker for Phil Lesh. “Parish” referring to the band’s stage manager Steve Parish. On the top of the cabinet is the handwritten notation “Property of Simon Babbs & Tom Bassett.”  With new custom road case decorated with stickers.    Speaker cabinet: 19 ¼ x 16 ½ x 30 in.  Road case: 22 x 19 ¾ x 33 ½ in.

title: U2
description_block: 12 x 12 in. folded (24 x 12 in. unfolded).   vinyl insert signed by U2. Black-and-white landscape poster of the band on recto and lyrics on verso. title: Fleetwood Mac
description_block: 29 ¾ x 20 ¼ in. Original mechanical artwork for Fleetwood Mac’s iconic 1977 masterpiece,  . The artwork featuring black and white photographs by Herbert Worthington III. Design and layout by Desmond Strobel and calligraphy by Larry Vigon of Vigon Nahas Vigon. The mechanical artwork comprises two separate pieces of illustration board; each containing two photographs.   First illustration board comprises the front cover featuring Mick Fleetwood and Stevie Nicks striking the now iconic pose. Nicks in her supernatural “Rhiannon” persona. Mick Fleetwood wears black waistcoat, matching trousers, long stockings and ballet slippers. Fleetwood wearing his now infamous wooden balls with chains hanging from his waist that Fleetwood yanked out of a toilet tank years earlier and became his Talisman. Board also features back cover artwork with Worthington’s contact sheets and collage of various photographs, including outtakes from the session; conveying casualness and intimacy not typically used on album art. Overlay of onionskin paper with notes in red marker and black and blue ballpoint.   Second illustration board featuring gatefold artwork; two black and white photographs including outtakes from the session; comprising collage and contact prints by Worthington. With onion skin paper with notes in brown marker and black ballpoint, detailing retouching and printers instructions for Warner Brothers’ production department.

title: Jerrel Jernigan Game-Used Rookie Season New York Giants Jersey
description_block: Jerrel Jernigan wore this offered New York Giants jersey on Oct. 16 during his rookie season and the Giants Super Bowl-winning season of 2011. In the Giants' 27-24 victory over the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium, Jernigan was targeted one time and did not record any catches in the game. In his rookie season, Jernigan appeared in eight games, primarily used as a return specialist. He returned 8 kickoffs for 186 yards. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. The base of the jersey's V-neck collar is an NFL Shield patch, which appears above a Giants logo. Accompanying the jersey is a COA from J.O. Sports Co. (LN86894) for authenticity of game use on the Oct. 16, 2011 game.

title: James Harrison Game-Used, Signed, Inscribed Collection (3) - Featuring Jersey, Gloves, Cleats
provenance: Letter of Provenance signed by James Harrison
description_block: Presented is a collection of James Harrison game-used memorabilia from the Steelers' game against the Oakland Raiders in Week 9 of the 2015 NFL season on Nov. 8, 2015. Harrison recorded 2 combined tackles (1 solo) while playing in 56 percent of the team's defensive snaps as the Steelers defeated the Raiders, 38-35. The lot includes a black Steelers home jersey, which features all numbering and lettering in tackle twill, with team-appropriate patches and player-specific tagging throughout. Accompanying the jersey is a pair of Under Armour gloves and black and yellow Under Armour football cleats. All three items have been signed by Harrison; Harrison has penned his flowing signature in black ink within the "9" of the number "92" on the jersey's back, as well as across the palm of the left glove and the medial side of the right cleat (in silver marker). Accompanying each signature is an inscription that reads "2015 Game Used 11-8-15 vs. Raiders" in matching ink. All three items exhibit evidence of excellent game use. Letter of Provenance signed by James Harrison attesting to the lot's authenticity. A trio of LOAs from Beckett (AE20976 for jersey, AE20977 for glove, and AE20978 for cleat) and PSA/DNA (AP06958 for glove, AP06959 for jersey, and AP06960 for cleat) for signatures. Please note the Harrison Signed LOP incorrectly states the Steelers' game against the Oakland Raiders as "Nov. 8, 2017." Harrison's inscription correctly states the game as Nov. 8 of 2015. The title and description reflects the correct player inscription.

title: Miami Dolphins Game-Used Jersey
match_event: Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets on Nov. 4, 2018
description_block: Presented is a game-used Miami Dolphins home jersey used by Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick during Miami's Nov. 4, 2018 matchup against the New York Jets at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. This game occurred during Fitzpatrick's rookie season in Miami; in the game—a tight 13-6 defensive-minded victory for Miami—Fitzpatrick recorded six combined tackles, including three solo tackles while playing 98.5 percent of defensive snaps. The following season, Fitzpatrick was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers, where he remained until 2025 when he was traded back to Miami. The size 38 jersey features a "2018" flag on its collar tag and an NFL Shield emblem at the apex of the collar; "Miami" is stitched into the inside of the collar. All player numbers and letters are applied in tackle twill. The jersey displays soiling (including dirt and grass stains) commensurate with its use. The item comes with a PSA/DNA COA (2N53677) for the use, attributing the jersey's usage to Fitzpatrick's participation in the Dolphins 13 to 6 victory over the Jets on Nov. 4, 2018.

title: Eric Berry Game-Used, Signed Kansas City Chiefs Home Jersey
match_event: Oct. 11, 2015 - Kansas City Chiefs vs. Chicago Bears
description_block: Kansas City Chiefs star safety Eric Berry wore this Chiefs home jersey on Oct. 11, 2015, against the Chicago Bears at Arrowhead Stadium. The former Tennessee collegian recorded three tackles and two passes defended in Kansas City's narrow 18-17 loss. The 2015 season would prove to be one of the most important in Berry's career. He overcame a tragic diagnosis of Hodgkin's lymphoma in December 2014 to post a First-Team All-Pro season and take home NFL AP Comeback Player of the Year honors in 2015 after recording 61 tackles with a pair of interceptions and 10 passes defended. Berry—a College Football Hall of Famer—has signed the "9" digit on the back of this red jersey in black ink. A Lamar Hunt memorial patch is sewn on the chest. A size "42 L-BK" tag with an attached "+4 Length" tag is sewn on the back inside collar. The jersey shows light to moderate wear and is accompanied by a PSA/DNA COA (2N20971) covering both the game-use and Berry's signature.

title: 1977 Robin Cole Game-Used Rookie Season Pittsburgh Steelers Home Jersey
description_block: Presented is a Pittsburgh Steelers black home football jersey used by two-time Super Bowl champion Robin Cole during the 1977 NFL season, Cole's first season in the NFL, where he appeared in 8 games with 1 start and recorded 2 fumble recoveries and 1.5 sacks. Cole would spend 12 years in the NFL, 11 with the Steelers, where he would be a member of the Super Bowl-winning 1978 and 1979 teams. Cole finished his career with 29 sacks and 15 fumble recoveries in 166 regular season games. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. The front left tail of the jersey contains a Medalist Sand Knit size "50" manufacturer's tag adjacent to a white fabric year identification patch labeled "77" in black thread. Thread pulling is present across the jersey's nameplate. Digital Pittsburgh Steelers LOA (501180) for game use.

title: June 13, 2009 - Gary Sheffield Career Home Run #506 - Game-Used, Signed, Heavily Inscribed Louisville Slugger R161 Professional Model Bat
match_event: New York Yankees vs. New York Mets on June 13, 2009
description_block: Presented is a Louisville Slugger R161 professional model baseball bat used by former Major League slugger Garry Sheffield in a game between the New York Yankees and New York Mets on June 13, 2009, when he slugged his 506th career home run. The home run, a solo shot, occurred in the top of the seventh inning against Yankees pitcher Alfredo Aceves; Sheffield would only slug three more home runs for the rest of the season before retiring following the 2009 season. The offered bat measures 34.75 inches in length, weighs 34.5 ounces, and is uncracked with evidence of outstanding game use. A heavy coat of pine tar covers the lower portion of the handle. The knob has been wrapped with several layers of batting tape. The barrel displays several ball marks and stitch impressions, with white leather scuffing and green and blue ink transfers throughout. Cleat impressions are also evident. The bat has been signed by Sheffield, who has penned his flowing signature in silver marker across the barrel; Sheffield has also inscribed "Career Homerun #506 vs. New York Yankees 6/13/09 Pitcher Alfredo Aceves." LOA from PSA/DNA (1B08870) with the highest possible grade of GU 10 for game use. MLB Authenticated Hologram (LH198816) for game use and signature. LOA from Beckett for signature.

title: 2001 Ichiro Suzuki Game-Used, Signed Rookie Season Seattle Mariners Home Jersey
provenance: Letter of Provenance from Yu Fukushima
description_block: Ichiro Suzuki's legacy as Japan's greatest baseball product has finally been challenged by the utter dominance of Shohei Ohtani in today's game, but that shouldn't discredit the immediate impact Ichiro had on the sport when he arrived in North America ahead of the 2001 MLB season. Barred from joining Major League Baseball until 2001, Ichiro—who was just elected to baseball's Hall of Fame on his first ballot with 99.7% of the vote on Jan. 21, 2025—arrived with a slew of accolades and hardware, including seven Golden Glove Awards in Japan, three Pacific League MVPs, and a pair of Matsutaro Shoriki Awards. After his first season in Major League Baseball, Ichiro collected additional hardware in the form of the American League Rookie of the Year and MVP (the first and only player since Fred Lynn in 1975 to win both honors in a single season), a Gold Glove, and a Silver Slugger. Presented is a 2001 Ichiro Suzuki game-used Seattle Mariners home baseball jersey. To say Ichiro exceeded expectations would be a severe understatement. In 157 games with the Seattle Mariners during his debut campaign, Ichiro won the batting title with a .350 batting average and a league-leading 242 hits, as well as leading the league with 56 stolen bases. It wasn't long until Ichiro became an international sensation; when Major League Baseball allowed All-Star voting in Japan, Ichiro became the first rookie in baseball history to lead all players in All-Star Game voting. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. A 2001 MLB All-Star Game patch, commemorating the Midsummer Classic as it was hosted in Seattle that season, rests on the jersey's left sleeve. An American League centennial patch sits opposite on the right sleeve. The front left tail of the jersey contains a Russell Athletic MLB Authentic Collection manufacturer's tag with attached size "48" and "2001" flags. Affixed to the back of the jersey's collar is an MLB Batter logo. The jersey has been signed by Ichiro, who has penned his flowing signature in silver marker within the "5" of the number "51" on the jersey's back. According to MEARS, the jersey exhibits evidence of Moderate use with wear consistent with player and position. Also, according to MEARS, the lack of a USA flag patch on the back of the jersey "indicates jersey was worn prior to 09/11." LOA from MEARS (322164) with the highest possible grade of A10 for game use. Letter of Provenance from Yu Fukushima for authenticity. COA from Mill Creek Sports for game use and signature. Please note MEARS has evaluated and deemed this item as "game-used" with the grade of A10. MEARS evaluates game-used jerseys based on a 1-10 grading scale, with points assigned for attributes that include tagging, lettering, numbering, size, patches, materials, style, as well as provenance, supporting imagery, wear, and use. However, this designation from MEARS neither confirms nor guarantees a photo-match result. The sale of this lot is on an "as-is" basis, and the sale is final.

title: Van Jefferson Game-Used, Photo-Matched Pittsburgh Steelers Home Jersey

description_block: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Van Jefferson used this Steelers home jersey when he recorded 1 catch for 10 yards and a touchdown in the 27-14 Steelers victory over the Cleveland Browns in a Week 14 matchup on Dec. 8, 2024. Jefferson connected with former Steelers quarterback Russell Wilson in the third quarter to give the Steelers a 20-7 lead. The touchdown reception was Jefferson's second of the season; he would play in a total of 40 offensive snaps for the Steelers. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. A Steelers team patch sits on the jersey's upper left chest, and an NFL Shield patch sits on the base of the jersey's V-neck collar. The inside back of the jersey's collar displays a Nike Engineered size "40" manufacturer's patch with attached "2024" and "SHORT CAP" flags. Adjacent to the Nike patch is a black fabric patch labeled "GW-24" in yellow lettering. LOA from Davious Sports Photomatching (MM3390), who have conclusively photo-matched the jersey to the Dec. 8, 2024, game between the Steelers and Browns. Digital Steelers LOA (703338) for game use.

title: Jerry Rice Game-Used, Photo-Matched, Signed, Inscribed Oakland Raiders Home Jersey
match_event: Raiders vs San Diego Chargers, Nov. 18, 2001
description_block: Presented is an Oakland Raiders home football jersey used by Hall of Fame wide receiver Jerry Rice in a game between the Raiders and San Diego Chargers in Week 10 of the 2001 NFL regular season on Nov. 18, 2001. Rice was a dominant factor in the Raiders' offensive scheme; Rice and quarterback Rich Gannon connected 8 times for 131 yards and 3 touchdowns in the Raiders' 34-24 victory. Rice and Gannon first connected for a 12-yard score in the first quarter before Gannon found Rice with a 30-yard-deep ball and a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. The touchdowns were the 191st, 192nd, and 193rd receiving touchdowns in Rice's career. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. An NFL Shield patch sits on the base of the jersey's V-neck collar, and the front left tail of the jersey contains a Reebok manufacturer's tag with attached "3" L.B." and "42" flags. The inside back of the jersey's collar features a white fabric patch labeled "01-42" in black numbering. The jersey has been signed by Rice, who has penned his flowing signature in black marker within the "0" of the number "80" on the jersey's back; Rice has added the inscription "Raiders VS S.D. Chargers T.D. 191, 192, 193" in black marker across the "8." LOA from Resolution Photomatching (RJ0728213), which provides a conclusive ResMatch™ to the Nov. 18, 2021, game between the Raiders and Chargers. STICKER ONLY from Fanatics (B615627) for signature.

title: 2024 Aaron Judge Game-Used, Photo-Matched, Signed Nike Air Jordan Retro 11 Cleats - Matched to (5) Games - 3 Home Runs, 8 Hits, 7 RBIs - Davious Sports LOA, Fanatics COA, MLB Authenticated on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Presented is a pair of game-used and signed Nike Air Jordan Retro 11 cleats worn by New York Yankees superstar outfielder Aaron Judge, photo-matched to five games during the 2024 MLB season, which saw Judge win American League MVP and the Yankees win the pennant. The cleats were worn by the two-time league MVP during the following matchups (with the player's game stats highlighted): Totals: 5 wins, 8 for 19 with 3 home runs, a double, and 7 RBIs. The offered Nike Air Jordan Retro 11 cleats exhibit clay staining throughout and creasing on the toeboxes. Jordan Jumpman manufacturer's logos appear on the heels, tongues, and outsoles, with Nike Swoosh logos appearing on each metal spike. Judge has signed the right cleat, penning his flowing signature in silver marker across the toebox. Accompanying the cleats is an LOA from Davious Sports (MM3686), who have conclusively photo-matched the cleats to the aforementioned games. COA from Fanatics (RG13322132, QLC) and (RG13322133, MTH) for authenticity of game use. Affixed to the right cleat is an MLB Authenticated Hologram (YP573393, VQH) for authenticity of signature. Please note, Davious Sports mistakenly states Judge went 1 for 3 in the April 21, 2024 game against the Rays. According to both ESPN.com and baseball-reference.com, Judge went 1 for 4 in that game. The lot's description is consistent with information from these sources. Please note, the Hologram IDs on the Fanatics COA and stickers do not appear in the Fanatics Authentication site at this time.

title: World Series Game 7 - Carlos Correa Game-Used, Photo-Matched Houston Astros Road Jersey
description_block: Houston Astros star shortstop Carlos Correa used this offered Astros road jersey during the deciding Game 7 of the 2017 World Series on Nov. 1, 2017, at Dodger Stadium. In what was regarded as one of the greatest World Series in Major League Baseball history, the Astros came out ahead, defeating the Dodgers in Game 7 by a score of 5-1 to hoist their first World Series trophy in franchise history. Correa went 1 for 4 in the game, playing his usual swift defense at shortstop. Houston jumped all over Los Angeles in the game, scoring five runs in the first two innings off Dodgers' starter Yu Darvish. That would be all Houston needed, with Charlie Morton pitching 4.0 innings in relief to secure the victory. The offered road jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. The jersey's upper left chest features a Houston Strong patch, worn to show solidarity and support for the city after the devastation of Hurricane Harvey in Aug. of 2017. An Astros logo patch and a Majestic manufacturer's logo appear on the left sleeve, opposite a 2017 MLB World Series patch on the right sleeve. The jersey's front left tail features a size "46" MLB Authentic Collection Majestic manufacturer's tag, with the inside of the jersey containing a "2017 PROP OF HOUSTON 46TC -1.5 S ASTROS" MLB Authentic Collection Majestic barcode sticker (HUAA). An MLB Batter Logo rests above the nameplate on the jersey's back. Accompanying the jersey is an LOA from Sports Investors (250822M1), who have conclusively photo-matched the jersey to Game 7 of the 2017 World Series against the Dodgers.

description_block: Presented is an SSK professional model glove game-used by Padres superstar Fernando Tatis Jr., ResMatched™ to six games and likely photo-matched to six games during his rookie season in 2019, including his MLB debut on March 28, 2019. The glove was worn by the three-time All-Star during the following matchups (with the player's game stats highlighted): ResMatch™: Likely Photo-match: Tatis Jr. impressed during his rookie campaign, recording a Triple Crown slash line of .317/22/53 with 16 stolen bases in 84 games. description_block: NBA icon, Hall of Famer, and basketball icon Michael Jordan, returning from a fractured navicular bone in his left foot suffered in the third game of the season, used this pair of Nike Air Jordan 1 basketball sneakers during the 1985-86 NBA regular season, his second season with the Chicago Bulls. Jordan's injury robbed the basketball world of what might have been an electric sophomore campaign; limited to only 18 games, Jordan made 7 starts and averaged 22.7 points per game with 3.6 total rebounds and 2.9 assists. Despite being without one of the most electric young talents in the NBA, the Bulls reached the Eastern Conference First Round; in three games against the Boston Celtics, Jordan averaged 43.7 points per game with 6.3 total rebounds and 5.7 assists as the Bulls bowed out of the playoffs. One characteristic that can be found within this pair that makes these sneakers so unique is the modification made to accommodate Jordan's return from injury. The sneakers feature a harness to provide support to his foot and ankle. Outside of these modifications, the sneakers exhibit all expected qualities that have made this pair one of the most recognizable sneakers in the world: a red/white/black colorway matching the primary colors of the Bulls and the Air Jordan emblem embossed across the lateral side of each ankle. Add the fact that Jordan has signed each sneaker, penning his flowing signature in black marker across the medial side of each ankle, and you have a pair of Air Jordan 1s personalized for "MJ" and by "MJ." The sneakers have been apparently photo-matched to a March 21, 1986, game by Sports Investors Authentication. A preview of their matchup in the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs, the Bulls fell to the Celtics on that date by the score of 126-105. Jordan, in his fourth game since returning from injury, recorded 20 points in only 16 minutes of playing time with 2 total rebounds and 1 assist. While the lack of clarity in the photos prevents Sports Investors from being absolutely certain "that these shoes are photo matched," evidence of game use, as is consistent with sneakers worn during a single game, is certain: creasing and scuffing on the uppers and tread wear on the outsoles. Light decomposition in the black leather near the ankle is also evident. Very light oxidation in the midsoles, a trait common with sneakers from this era, is also evident. The interior of the sneakers is stamped: the right sneaker is stamped "13 ½ 850102-TYPS," and the left sneaker is stamped "13 850102-TYPS," confirming Jordan's characteristic of wearing two different-sized sneakers and that these are player samples manufactured at the Tong Yang factory in 1985. There's no denying the Air Jordan 1 is the most iconic basketball sneaker of all time, bold and innovatively designed to create a statement of rebellion and self-expression while ushering in a new era of footwear design ruled by the iconic Air Jordan brand. Such was the success around the brand's marketing that they blew past the expected $3 million in sales to net $126 million within the first year. Sports Investors Authentication considers the sneakers to be "in excellent condition compared to most Air Jordan 1 gamers" they've examined. LOA from Sports Investors Authentication (250622M1) for game use and an apparent photo-match to March 21, 1986. LOA from JSA and Beckett for signatures. Please note that the item was recently authenticated by JSA and Beckett. The LOAs will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.
