title: Bobby Hull Game-Used, Photo-Matched Canada National Team Jersey - Tournament Finals Game vs. Czechoslovakia on Sept. 15, 1976 - MeiGray LOA on Goldin Auctions
match_event: Canada Cup Final vs. Czechoslovakia on Sept. 15, 1976
description_block: The significance of the 1976 Canada Cup cannot be overstated. It was the first tournament that featured the best of the world's best in hockey; up to that point, Team Canada faced a serious disadvantage in international tournaments as they were restricted from using players from the NHL. Meanwhile, other European teams managed to circumnavigate this restriction by masking the status of their best players. This came to a head in 1970, with Team Canada refusing to play international ice hockey competitions until they could use their top players like European countries could. After years of negotiation, Canada agreed to return to international competitions in exchange for being able to use NHL players; in a further gesture of goodwill, the 1976 Canada Cup was created as the first international competition to meet these new agreements. With Team Canada now fully equipped with a team of amateurs and professionals of their choosing, they went on to display some of their best international hockey action throughout the six-team round robin tournament. When Canada reached the finals to face Czechoslovakia, more than 10.5 million people were estimated to have tuned in for the game (a number that was roughly half of all Canadians in 1976). Presented is a Canada National Team hockey jersey used by Hockey Hall of Famer and one of the greatest goal scorers in the history of the NHL, Bobby Hull, during the 1976 Canada Cup Final between Czechoslovakia and Canada, a best-of-three series that saw the Canadians sweep both games with a 6-0 victory on Sept. 13 and a 5-4 overtime victory on Sept. 15, 1976. Hull, who was accounted as one of the tournament's leading scorers with 5 goals and 3 assists for 8 points in 7 games, used this jersey during Canada's overtime victory on Sept. 15. Featuring sealed numbering, lettering, and team logos on the front, back, and shoulders, the jersey displays an alternate captain's "A" letter stitched on the upper left chest. Attached to the inside of the jersey's collar is an "AK" size "46" manufacturer's tag with wash instructions. The jersey exhibits heavy staining from use and comes with an LOA from MeiGray (160697), who have conclusively photo-matched the jersey to the second game of the best-of-three 1976 Canada Cup Final between Canada and Czechoslovakia on Sept. 15, 1976. The jersey has been photo-matched to a 1992 Future Trends Hockey Card #178 'Last Time for #9' and an 8-by-10-inch photograph of Hull celebrating a goal; both images were taken during Team Canada's Game 2 victory at the Montreal Forum in Montreal, Canada, on Sept. 15, 1976.

title: 2006 Roger Federer Match-Used, Signed White Nike Polo
description_block: Presented is a match-used Roger Federer white Nike polo shirt used during the revered Swiss legend's triumphant, title-winning run at the 2006 Swiss Indoors tournament (known as the "Davidoff Swiss Indoors" at the time for sponsorship purposes) in his hometown of Basel, Switzerland. Federer has signed the shirt on its chest in black ink. In late October 2006, after a ludicrously successful season that saw him appear in the final of all four Grand Slam tournaments (winning three: the Australian Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open), Federer returned to his hometown of Basel capture a title that was conspicuously absent from his sprawling trophy case: the Swiss Indoors. Federer had previously been defeated in the finals of the 2000 and 2001 editions of the event, and had only participated in the event one more time (2003) since winning his maiden Grand Slam event at the 2003 Wimbledon Championships. Federer—who was the owner of nine Slam titles at the time of this event—was determined to win on home soil, and he did just that, defeating Tomas Zib, Guillermo García López, and David Ferrer in straight sets before besting Paradorn Srichaphan in three sets in the semifinals. This set up a final matchup with the tournament's reigning champion, Fernando González. Federer defeated the Chilean in three straight sets, winning his first title at the Swiss event. He would go on to win the tournament nine additional times (including in 2019, when his straight sets victory over Alex de Minaur served as the final ATP title of his career), an all-time record at the event. This was Federer's 11th title of 2006 and the 44th of his career. The offered match-used Federer Nike polo is white with black stripes at the shoulders and on the lower back. The size-large shirt features a black Nike "Swoosh" logo over the left breast and a three-button placket below the collar. Federer has signed the shirt directly below its three-button enclosure. The item comes with a COA from the Roger Federer Foundation for the use and an LOA from Beckett for Federer's signature. Please note that the item was recently authenticated by Beckett. The LOA will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.

title: Michael Jordan Game-Used, Photo-Matched, Signed Chicago Bulls Home Jersey
description_block: The horizon of 1998 promised many things for the Chicago Bulls and their fanbase: a chance at their second threepeat of the decade, marking one of the greatest organizational runs in the history of the National Basketball Association while simultaneously foretelling the end of a golden era of Chicago basketball. No matter how you chalked it up, the Bulls' run through the 1998 playoffs promised to be bittersweet, regardless of the outcome. Presented is a Chicago Bulls home basketball jersey used by NBA Hall of Famer and basketball icon Michael Jordan in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals at the United Center in Chicago, IL, on May 6, 1998. The Bulls had already aced their first four games of the postseason, having swept the New Jersey Nets in three games during the Eastern Conference First Round before taking Game 1 of the Semifinals against the Charlotte Hornets. Jordan, to no one's surprise, led all players with 22 points in the game while adding a game-high 6 assists and 5 total rebounds in just under 40 minutes of playing time in the Bulls' narrow 78-76 loss. The Bulls would settle for the gentleman's sweep by taking the next three games to advance to the Eastern Conference Finals to face off against the Indiana Pacers in one of the hardest-fought series in basketball playoffs history. The Chicago Bulls' playoff run to their third consecutive NBA title in 1998 truly proved to be that dynasty's "Last Dance." Jordan announced he was retiring from the league following his sixth NBA title, a decision that would last until 2001, when he returned to the league as a member of the Washington Wizards. Hall of Fame head coach Phil Jackson resigned from his position before joining the Los Angeles Lakers in 1999, and the rest of the team was broken up: Hall of Famer Scottie Pippen was traded to the Houston Rockets, Dennis Rodman joined the Lakers, and role players Steve Kerr, Luc Longley, Scott Burrell, Jud Buechler, and Joe Kleine also departed. The Golden Era of Chicago Bulls basketball had come to an end. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. An NBA Logoman patch sits on the jersey's upper left chest, and the front left tail of the jersey contains a Nike size "50" manufacturer's patch with an attached "LENGTH +4" flag and "CHICAGO BULLS" and "NBA AUTHENTICS" tags. The jersey has been signed by Jordan, who has penned his flowing signature in black marker within the "2" of the number "23" on the jersey's back. LOAs from MeiGray and MeiGray Photomatching (157063), who have conclusively photo-matched the jersey to Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals between the Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets on May 6, 1998. description_block: Ichiro Suzuki's legacy as Japan's greatest baseball product has finally been challenged by the utter dominance of Shohei Ohtani in today's game, but that shouldn't discredit the immediate impact Ichiro had on the sport when he arrived in North America ahead of the 2001 MLB season. Barred from joining Major League Baseball until 2001, Ichiro—who was just elected to baseball's Hall of Fame on his first ballot with 99.7% of the vote on Jan. 21, 2025—arrived with a slew of accolades and hardware, including seven Golden Glove Awards in Japan, three Pacific League MVPs, and a pair of Matsutaro Shoriki Awards. After his first season in Major League Baseball, Ichiro collected additional hardware in the form of the American League Rookie of the Year and MVP (the first player since Fred Lynn in 1975 to win both honors in a single season), a Gold Glove, and a Silver Slugger. A 2001 Ichiro Suzuki game-used Seattle Mariners alternate baseball jersey and undershirt is presented. To say Ichiro exceeded expectations would be a severe understatement. In 157 games with the Seattle Mariners during his debut campaign, Ichiro won the batting title with a .350 batting average and a league-leading 242 hits, as well as leading the league with 56 stolen bases. A 2001 MLB All-Star Game patch, commemorating the Midsummer Classic as it was hosted in Seattle that season, rests on the jersey's left sleeve; when Major League Baseball allowed All-Star voting in Japan, Ichiro became the first rookie in baseball history to lead all players in All-Star Game voting. The front left tail of the jersey contains a Russell Athletic MLB Authentic Collection manufacturer's tag with an attached "2001" flag. The jersey has been signed by Ichiro, who has penned his flowing signature in silver marker across the back of the jersey below the number "51." Ichiro has added the inscription "01 ROY/MVP." Accompanying the jersey is an Asics long-sleeved undershirt also used by Ichiro during the 2001 season; the shirt features a white "51" tag on the front left tail. According to MEARS, the jersey exhibits evidence of Moderate use with wear consistent with player and position. LOA from MEARS (323135) with the grade of A10 for game use. COA from Mill Creek Sports for game-use authenticity for the undershirt. Please note MEARS has evaluated and deemed this item as “game-used” with the grade of A10. MEARS evaluates game-used jerseys based on a 1-10 grading scale, with points assigned for attributes that include tagging, lettering, numbering, size, patches, materials, style, as well as provenance, supporting imagery, wear, and use. title: 1967-68 Dan Issel Game-Used, Photo-Matched, Signed Kentucky Wildcats Jersey

description_block: Yes, this is a photo-matched gamer from the University of Kentucky men's all-time leading scorer and rebounder. Period. Full stop. Dan Issel netted 2,138 points for Adolph Rupp's Wildcats in only 3 seasons (back when NCAA freshman couldn't play varsity) and without a 3-point line. There's even a fabled Sports Illustrated story about the legendary UK coach predicting that prolific future during a timeout. Encouraging teammates to pass more to the underclassman Issel, Rupp himself said, "This guy is going to be Kentucky's all-time leading scorer by the time he's through here. I thought you might like to meet him." Just recently, the University unveiled a brand-new Issel statue outside Rupp Arena! The 6'8 center/forward cemented his legacy in the Bluegrass State by dominating professionally for the ABA's Kentucky Colonels. He holds the record for most points in an ABA season (2,538) and ranks second-best for career ABA points (12,823). Issel's Basketall Hall of Fame bio describes him as "one of the hardest working players in basketball history…the model of durability and consistency." Hence Issel's nickname: The Horse. This spectacular sophomore jersey has been matched to uniformed UK portraits of Issel and apparent matched to multiple UK games. It features a distinctive "Y" in "KENTUCKY" (with a horizontal buckle or crease to the letter itself), as well as a noticeably small distance between the upper-right of the second "4" in "44" to the second "K" in "KENTUCKY." According to Sports Investors, the King O'Shea size-48 jersey is an apparent match to 3 Wildcat games: 1) Feb. 3, 1968 vs. LSU (against rival Pete Maravich!); 2) Mar. 15, 1968 vs. Marquette (NCAA Tournament Round of 16 with Issel's then-career high 36 points); and 3) Mar. 16, 1968 vs. Ohio State (NCAA Tournament Elite Eight with 19 points, 8 rebounds). Additional provenance includes a pair of signed 16 x 20 action photos from the Kentucky/Marquette game; a signed 8 x 10 photo in uniform with Rupp; and a pair of Polaroids showing Issel autographing the jersey front. One of the finest Kentucky Wildcat vintage gamers ever to hit the auction block! LOAs from Sports Investors (for matching), Resolution (for matching) and Beckett (for autograph).

title: Barry Bonds 600th Career Home Run - Actual Game-Used OML Selig Baseball
condition: light clay staining with numerous scuffs
description_block: Regarded as the greatest hitter in the history of the MLB, the story of baseball cannot be told without a chapter—or perhaps a few—dedicated to the greatness of Barry Bonds. It was on Aug. 9, 2002, a cool night at Pacific Bell Park (now Oracle Park) in San Francisco, when Bonds joined baseball royalty. Presented is the Official Major League Allan H. Selig baseball hit for Barry Bonds' illustrious 600th career home run off Kip Wells. The stage was set as Bonds walked to the plate in the bottom of the sixth inning with the Giants trailing by two runs against his former team, the Pittsburgh Pirates. With a 2-1 count, Bonds got a fastball over the plate and blasted the offered ball to deep center field, clearing the wall with ease. Bonds rounded first base with his pointer finger in the air, as 41,897 fans roared in elation. Bonds stepped on home plate with his patented double finger point to the sky. On his way back to the dugout, he blew a kiss to his family, who was sitting in the front row behind home plate, eventually getting congratulated by his teammates as fireworks erupted in the San Francisco skyline. The ball traveled an estimated 421 feet and was Bonds' 33rd of the 2002 season. With the homer, Bonds became the fourth member of the 600 home run club, joining Hall of Famers Hank Aaron, Babe Ruth, and Willie Mays as the only other players to accomplish the historic feat at the time. Bonds also became the fastest player in MLB history to go from 500 home runs to 600 home runs, doing so in just 240 games. Bonds would go on to win his fourth National League Most Valuable Player award in 2002, the second of four consecutive MVP honors. He recorded an unprecedented .370/46/110 Triple Crown slash line, leading Major League Baseball in batting average, walks, on-base percentage, and slugging percentage. The Giants would lose the Aug. 9, 2002, contest 4-3 to the Pirates, but Bonds walked away with a winning achievement, nonetheless. The offered baseball exhibits light clay staining with numerous scuffs throughout, and fading is present on each of the blue stamps. Affixed to the ball is an MLB Authenticated Hologram (MR024402) for authenticity of game use for this historic moment.

title: 2015 Wimbledon Novak Djokovic Match-Worn Dual Signed Adidas Tennis Shoes
description_block: Presented is a pair of 2015 Wimbledon Novak Djokovic match-worn, twice-signed Adidas tennis shoes. Djokovic has signed each shoe on its respective outside panel near the toe. The Serbian icon's 2015 campaign was one of the greatest single years in tennis history. He started off by claiming the Australian Open title over his opponent in the final, Andy Murray. He then snatched up titles at Indian Wells, Miami, Monte-Carlo, and Italy before losing in the French Open final to Stan Wawrinka. Next up was the Wimbledon Championships, where Djokovic was the reigning champion. The number one seed, Djokovic largely breezed to the final save for a tense five-setter against South African serve specialist Kevin Anderson in round four; he otherwise defeated Philipp Kohlschreiber, Jarkko Nieminen, Bernard Tomic, Marin Cilic, and Richard Gasquet in straight sets to reach the final against the king of grass courts, Roger Federer. The first two frames of the final both went to tie-breakers: Djokovic snatched the first one easily with a 7-1 victory in the breaker, while Federer outlasted his opponent in a see-sawing 12-10 tiebreaker to level the match at one set a piece. Djokovic—at this stage the younger, hungrier athlete—won the final two frames without the need of a tiebreaker to take the match—and the Wimbledon men's singles title—in four sets. His historic season was far from over, as he won additional titles at the US Open (staking his claim with three of year's four Grand Slam titles while making all four finals), China Open, Shanghai Masters, Paris Masters, and ATP World Tour Finals. He finished the season with 11 titles, including three major titles and a record six Masters 1000 titles. He went 82-6 in matchplay for the season, a personal record for single-season victories. The offered 2015 Wimbledon Djokovic match-worn Adidas tennis shoes are primarily white (in accordance with the tournament's dress code), with three black Adidas stripes on each side panel and an orange detail at the heel and tongue. The size 11.5 shoes feature Djokovic's personal logo on the outside ankle portion of each sneaker; the left sneaker features a white dove logo on the inside ankle portion, while the right sneaker features a Reiki power symbol in that same spot. Djokovic has signed each shoe on its respective outside panel near the toe. The shoes come with an LOA from MEARS (323138), which has described them as displaying "heavy" wear and assessed them as "Authentic." Additionally, the shoes come with two LOAs from Beckett for the signatures. Please note that this item is accompanied by an LOA from MEARS, which has deemed it "match-worn." description_block: Presented is a game-used Louisville Slugger Hillerich & Bradsby R195 professional model baseball bat used by baseball's all time hits king, Pete Rose, between 1977 and 1979. Few ballplayers are as intrinsically associated with the art of hitting as Rose, the owner of a career .302 batting average and an MLB-record 4,256 hits, and his game-used bats (especially those displaying the level of use exhibited by the offered example) form an important part of any advanced collection of game-used baseball memorabilia. From 1977 to 1979, Rose batted a collective .315 with 610 total hits, 129 doubles (including an MLB-best 51 in 1978), 175 RBI, and 20 home runs. He made an All-Star team in each of those three seasons and finished in the top 15 in NL MVP balloting each time, as well (amazingly, over those three seasons, he only struck out 104 total times; more than 50 batters have struck out more times in the on-going 2025 season alone). After playing the 1977 and 1978 seasons with the Reds franchise with which he debuted in 1963, Rose donned a different hue of red in 1979 for the Philadelphia Phillies. Sadly, Rose—one of the most accomplished hitters in baseball history—passed away in 2024 at the age of 83. The ash bat is uncracked, weighs 33.8 ounces, and measures 35.0 inches in length. According to the item's accompanying PSA/DNA LOA (G55804), the bat "exhibits evidence of outstanding use," including "many ball marks and ball stitch impressions" on the barrel. Cleat marks and red and green bat rack streaks are also visible. The LOA notes that the "right barrel appears to have been cleaned with alcohol which is a well-known Rose characteristic," additionally mentioning that a "painted image of Rose has been removed from the front barrel." PSA/DNA has assigned this bat a stellar grade of "PSA/DNA GU 10." The bat also comes with LOAs from PSA/DNA (AP06798) and Beckett (AE20945) for Rose's signature.

Roger Federer ultimately won the event. Murray had suffered a lingering hip injury before the tournament began and chose to withdraw from the year's remaining tournaments to recuperate. Judge, who hit his 350th home run—a two-run shot—off Cubs pitcher Brad Keller in the bottom of the ninth inning in a 5-2 loss, did so in only his 1,088th career game. A two-time American League MVP, the 2017 American League Rookie of the Year, and the owner of the single-season home run record in the junior circuit, Judge has fast-tracked his way to a spot in Cooperstown. title: 1948 Eddie Robinson Game-Used Cleveland Indians Home Jersey and Pants - World Championship Season - William F. Henderson LOA on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Former Cleveland Indians first baseman Eddie Robinson wore this Cleveland Indians jersey and pants during the 1948 season, the one that saw the Indians post a record of 97-58-1, with Lou Boudreau's team securing a World Series in six games against the Boston Braves for their first title in 28 years. Robinson was instrumental to their success, batting .254 with 83 RBIs and 16 home runs. As stated by noted game-used jersey expert William Henderson, '...but it is the finest example of an original Indians uniform from their World Series championship season that I have ever seen.' As the Indians were notoriously frugal and often recycled jerseys into the minor leagues, which were then worn to the point of destruction, the fact that it has remained in its original and unrestored state is a wonder in itself. The jersey is made of heavyweight wool flannel, typical of exemplars from the late 1940s. The seven-button jersey features navy piping sewn to the placket and collar. "Indians" is stitched across the chest in thick felt. The original Chief Wahoo patch is sewn onto the left sleeve. Robinson’s number "3" is double-stitched on the back in felt. Notably, the construction of the jersey is unusual in that it was made without any sleeve seams and instead has a stitched seam running up the middle of the back, a characteristic of Indians exemplars from the period. The inside collar features a Wilson tag with an adjacent white swatch labeled "48," in black. "Robinson" is stitched in cursive on a white swatch below. The jersey, especially given the Indians’ history, is in "very good condition," as per the Henderson LOA that accompanies, but exhibits minor insect damage, several small holes on the jersey where the fabric is perforated, evidence of moth damage, with minor foxing on the jersey. A few dark spots and holes caused by sweat and mold spores which occurs in storage. The pants feature a linen-lined waistband with parallel stitched "Rub Strips," designed to keep the shirt tucked in tight. A faint number "4" is penned inside one of the inner pockets by an unknown hand. A Wilson tag appears on the inside waistband with a size tag "36" adjacent. The pants exhibit wear and stress around the pocket edges, some red fabric staining at the leg openings from the socks, and multiple major team repairs to the right knee. Still, when one considers the rarity of an Indians uniform from the period and its condition, this makes the perfect addition to any serious game-used collection. Accompanied by an LOA from noted game-used jersey expert Bill Henderson for the game use.

Henderson concludes his evaluation with, "This is pitcher Dave Leonhard's 1969 home game-worn Orioles jersey, with its original tagging and front cresting, showing a restored player name on back and restored numbers on both front and back." title: 1985 Pete Rose Signed Cincinnati Reds Home Game Jersey with Pants - William F. Henderson LOA, Beckett LOA
description_block: A 1985 Pete Rose Cincinnati Reds home game jersey and pair of pants are presented. In the twilight of his career at the age of 44, the 1985 MLB season marked the final season in which Rose recorded several accomplishments. It was the 23rd and final consecutive season in which Rose had at least 100 hits in a campaign, and it also saw Rose swat the final 2 of his 160 career home runs. On Sept. 11, 1985 (or Sept. 8, depending on if you adhere to the statistical error where two of Cobb's hits were counted twice), he surpassed Ty Cobb's all-time hits record with the 4,192nd hit of his career. 1985 also marked the final time Rose managed to play in more than 100 games. His retirement in 1986 saw "Charlie Hustle" set Major League records in games played (3,562), plate appearances (15,890), at-bats (14,053), and, of course, hits with 4,256. The offered jersey is a size "43" white pullover-style Cincinnati Reds home uniform manufactured by Goodman and Sons of Los Angeles California and featuring all numbering and lettering in tackle twill. The front left tail of the jersey contains a W.A. Goodman size "43" manufacturer's tag with wash instructions; Rose, taking advantage of the burgeoning collector hobby and the high demand for his own gamers, had the manufacturing company only tag the jerseys issued to him for game use with the size "43"; a true measuring of the jersey reveals it is a size 44. Adjacent to the manufacturer's tag is a chain-stitched year tag labeled "85" in red lettering, an uncommon feature for Reds uniforms from that year. William F. Henderson, in his Letter of Authenticity, surmises that the embroidered tag "was added after the fact, or perhaps by Rose and his agents trying to make their [collectible] look even better without regard to matching exemplars compared to other 1985-used Reds team jerseys." Accompanying the jersey is a pair of Goodman-tagged size "34" pants. The inside of the elastic waistband features a strip tag labeled "ROSE 34-28.5 ST 2 '85" in red numbering and lettering. The pants are of matching style and vintage as the jersey but lack any evidence of use. LOA from William F. Henderson (25-0813J02), who concludes that "this is a team issued and Pete Rose jersey from the 1985 season showing appropriate light use; the pants do not show use." The jersey has been signed by Rose, who has penned his flowing signature in black marker across the upper left chest; LOA from Beckett for signature. Please note that the item was recently authenticated by Beckett. The LOA will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.

Nurmagomedov would capture the UFC Lightweight Title in his next bout against Al Iaquinta; he retired in 2020 with a perfect 29-0 record, having defended his lightweight belt three times. title: 2002 Roland Garros Serena Williams Match Worn Signed Cameroon National Tennis Dress
description_block: Presented is a 2002 French Open Serena Williams match-worn Puma tennis dress decked out in the colorway of the Cameroon national soccer team's kits from that same year. Williams has signed the dress in black ink in the center. The younger Williams sister entered the 2002 French Open as the third seed behind the year's reigning Australian Open champion Jennifer Capriati and Serena's sister Venus. She breezed through the first three years, not dropping a set prior to the opening frame of her fourth round match against Vera Zvonareva (after losing the first set, Williams dropped only one additional game in the match). In the quarterfinals, she defeated wildcard Mary Pierce before defeating WTA No. 1 Jennifer Capriati in three sets in the semifinals. This set up a much-anticipated Williams vs. Williams showdown in the final, with Serena lining up opposite her older sister Venus (in their lone Grand Slam final match before the 2002 French Open, Venus briskly defeated her younger sister in straight sets in the 2001 US Open final). In the final, Serena marked herself as the player of the moment and the future, besting her sister in straight sets to win her first Roland-Garros title and her second major title overall. She would not lose another Grand Slam match until the following year's French Open semifinals, concluding a run of four straight Grand Slam title victories that was widely dubbed the "Serena Slam." This match-worn dress (paying tribute to the 2002 Cameroon men's soccer team, a Puma-affiliated squad that was playing in the World Cup during that year's French Open event) matches the style of outfit that Williams wore in the first two rounds of the 2002 French Open; thereafter, following mild controversy in the press, Williams changed to a black outfit for the remainder of the tournament (similarly, Cameroon was not allowed to wear its sleeveless kits at the 2002 FIFA World Cup due to FIFA regulations). Despite its brief usage on court, the Cameroon-style dress is widely regarded as one of the most striking and stylish tennis outfits of all time. The dress utilizes a sleeveless design and is predominantly green with yellow and red trim. A Cameroon Football Association patch appears near the bottom hem, directly across from a white Puma logo. A gold lion (a symbol of Cameroonian football) appears near the right shoulder, directly across from another white Puma logo. The Cameroonian flag appears on the back of the dress, near the collar. The dress comes with an LOA from Puma for the use as well as an LOA from Beckett for Williams' signature. title: Nico Hoerner Game-Used, Signed Chicago Cubs Cap - Anderson Authentics LOA on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Presented is a signed Chicago Cubs cap game-used by Cubs' middle infielder Nico Hoerner. The offered cap features moderate use with sweat and dirt stains from use. The front of the cap features a Cubs logo, with a New Era manufacturer's logo appearing on the left side and an MLB Batter Logo on the back. The inside of the cap includes an MLB Authentic Collection Official On-Field Cap tag, a New Era manufacturer's tag, and a 7½ size tag. Hoerner's number "2" has been handwritten in black marker on the inside of the cap by an unknown hand. Hoerner has signed the offered cap, penning his flowing signature in silver marker on the bill, including his number "2." Accompanying the cap is an LOA from Anderson Authentics (6001) for authenticity of game use and signature.

Hill helped the 2021 Kansas City Chiefs reach the AFC Championship, where they fell to the Cincinnati Bengals. Known for his blazing speed and run-after-the-catch ability, Hill is regarded as one of the greatest receivers of his era. The offered red and white Adidas cleats exhibit scuffing and staining from use. Adidas manufacturer's logos appear on the tongues, outsoles, and toeboxes of each cleat, with "ADIZERO" appearing on the lateral sides. According to MEARS, the size "10" cleats exhibit heavy wear. description_block: Presented is a 1986-88 Toninho Cerezo Sampdoria match jersey. The Brazilian defensive midfielder recorded 8 goals in 85 matches for Sampdoria. He would go on to help the club finish at the top of the table in Serie A during the 1990-91 season. The offered jersey features numbering in tackle twill. A Phonola sponsor logo appears on the center chest with a Sampdoria team crest on the left sleeve. An NR Classico manufacturer's logo is present on the upper left chest. According to MEARS, the jersey exhibits moderate use with wear consistent with player and position. LOA from MEARS (322459), who have assessed the jersey as Authentic.

title: 1989-90 Chicago Bulls Home Uniform Shorts - MEARS Authentic on Goldin Auctions
description_block: A pair of 1989-90 Chicago Bulls home uniform shorts is presented. The Bulls won 55 games during the regular season before a deep playoff run all the way to the Eastern Conference Finals, where they fell to the Detroit Pistons in seven games. Manufactured by Sand-Knit/MacGregor, the offered shorts feature a red/white/black color scheme and are constructed out of mesh with elastic material. Team logos are present on each leg, and an NBA Logoman patch sits on the right sleeve. The inside back of the short's waistband features a size "36" Sand-Knit manufacturer's tag, plus white fabric patches labeled "1'' HR" and "2''LI." According to MEARS, the shorts exhibit evidence of Light wear. LOA from MEARS (322525), who have assessed the shorts as Authentic.

description_block: Offered is a pair of 2006 Dwight Howard twice-signed Adidas Team USA sneakers. The size 18 sneakers display moderate wear and are accompanied by an LOA from MEARS, assessing them as "Authentic." Additionally, PSA/DNA STICKERS ONLY (K98083, K98084) cover Howard's signatures.

title: Dec. 2, 2022 - Zion Williamson Game-Used, Signed, Inscribed Nike Jordan Zion 2 Sneakers - Double-Double - Game-High 30 Points, Game-High 15 Rebounds, Team-High 8 Assists, 2 Steals - Fanatics COA on Goldin Auctions
match_event: Game against the San Antonio Spurs on Dec. 2, 2022
description_block: Presented is a pair of Nike Jordan Zion 2 basketball sneakers used by the New Orleans Pelicans' first overall pick from the 2019 NBA Draft and All-Star power forward Zion Williamson in a game against the San Antonio Spurs on Dec. 2, 2022 during the 2022-23 NBA regular season. Williamson was an unstoppable force in the Pelicans' 117-99 victory over the Spurs as he recorded a double-double with a game-high 30 points, a game-high 15 rebounds, and a team-high 8 assists. Williamson's dominance was on full display in the third quarter, where he scored 15 of his 30 total points in less than 10 minutes of playing time. The offered sneakers are predominantly black with gray and neon green accent designs and have been signed by Williamson. Williamson has penned his flowing signature in silver marker across the toe box of the right sneaker. The left toe box contains the inscription "GU 12/2/22, 30 pts, 15 Rebs, 8 ast." Williamson's personalized logo is present on each tongue, and the Nike Jumpman logo is present on each heel. Manufacturer's tags labeled "PROMO" in black lettering are attached to the underside of each tongue; each tag indicates the sneakers as size "M15." COA from Fanatics (HH98504990, ZSG, HH98504992, HCS) for game use and signature.

title: 2007 Kobe Bryant Game-Used Nike Zoom Kobe II Sneakers - MEARS Authentic on Goldin Auctions
description_block: A pair of 2007 Kobe Bryant game-used Nike Zoom Kobe II basketball sneakers is presented. The Nike Zoom Kobe II sneakers, the second iteration of the Kobe-exclusive signature series, saw improvement from its flagship design by proving lighter and less bulky than their predecessors. The sneakers debuted during the 2006-2007 NBA season; for the second consecutive season, Kobe led all players in scoring by averaging 31.6 points per game while adding 5.7 total rebounds and 5.4 assists in 77 games played. The offered sneakers feature a white/yellow/purple colorway with size "14" "SALES CFM SAMPLE" Nike manufacturer's tags attached to the interior. Nike logo branding and Kobe's personalized sheath logo are present throughout. According to MEARS, the sneakers exhibit evidence of Light wear. LOA from MEARS (322579), who have assessed the sneakers as Authentic. Please note MEARS has evaluated and deemed this item as “game-worn” with the assessment of "Authentic." Garcia was the first American boxer to ever be featured in a Gatorade commercial campaign. The offered Nike Flywire training boots display a unique red/white/blue/green colorway, and feature a painted "Grinch," decal on the outside of each shoe. A Nike logo decal rests on the inside face of the right shoe. A Nike manufacturer size flag is affixed to the inside of the boot. According to MEARS, the boots exhibit heavy wear. The boots come with an LOA from MEARS (323122) and have been assessed Authentic.

title: 1983-86 Darrell Walker New York Knicks Game-Worn Road Uniform Shorts - MEARS Authentic on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Presented is a pair of 1983-86 Darrell Walker New York Knicks game-worn road uniform shorts. Walker was drafted 12th overall in the 1983 NBA Draft by the Knicks, playing with the team until 1986. He recorded 10.6 points, 4.2 assists, and 2.7 rebounds per game in 245 games with New York. Walker had a 10-year NBA career, winning a championship with the Chicago Bulls in 1993. The offered road uniform shorts are mesh with elastic at the waist. A Knicks logo appears on the left leg, with Walker's number "4" appearing on the right leg. The inside of the waistband contains a "Designed and Tailored…" tag and a size "34" Medalist Sand-Knit manufacturer's tag. According to MEARS, the shorts exhibit heavy wear. description_block: Presented is a pair of circa 1999 Carlos Delgado game-used Adidas cleats. description_block: Presented are a pair of 2023-24 Player-Issued Nike Air Jordan XXXVII Hare JT P Sneakers signed by NBA superstar Jayson Tatum. Tatum has penned his black ink signature across the toe box of each sneaker (2 signatures). The offered sneakers feature a white/black/mint colorway, with Air Jordan logos on each outside heel. description_block: Presented is a 1997 Jerry Rice game-used and signed Nike cleat. In his age 35 season, Rice appeared in two games for the 49ers in the 1997 NFL season. title: A 1990 Skybox Michael Jordan Signed Autograph Basketball Card No. 41 (PSA 9 MINT AUTO)
provenance: Autograph obtained from Jordan by Make-A-Wish child in 1992 at Chicago Stadium
description_block:
A 1990 Skybox Michael Jordan Signed Autograph Basketball Card No. 41 (PSA 9 MINT AUTO)
On February 17, 2023, as he turned 60, Michael Jordan marked the milestone in signature fashion by making history off the court. He donated a record-setting $10 million to Make-A-Wish America, the largest single gift the organization has ever received.
Jordan’s connection to Make-A-Wish stretches back to 1989, when he granted his very first wish. In the decades since, he has brought joy to children around the world, turning fleeting moments into lifelong memories.
One of those moments came on January 25, 1992. Before the Chicago Bulls defeated the Houston Rockets 114–100, Jordan took time to meet a young fan from Michigan in the Bulls’ locker room at Chicago Stadium. What followed wasn’t just a meet-and-greet, it was an unforgettable, deeply personal experience. The boy, battling Non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, spent time with his hero in a private autograph session, sharing cards and memorabilia that Jordan carefully signed.
Even amid game-day responsibilities, like distributing his allotment of tickets, Jordan remained fully present. He joked, laughed, and, most importantly, offered words of encouragement that left a lasting impact.
That encounter became more than a cherished memory. It became a source of strength. More than three decades later, the young boy is now a man who continues to win his fight.
Now, pieces of that extraordinary day – those signed cards, each authenticated and graded by PSA, are being shared with the collecting world, carrying with them a story of resilience, generosity, and the enduring power of a simple wish.

auction_title: Sale 6514 - Sports Memorabilia: Featuring The Baseball Card Collection of David Eisenhower
title: A 1906 Chicago Baseball Champions Gold and Diamond Medallion Presented to Cubs Outfielder Billy Maloney
description_block:
A 1906 Chicago Baseball Champions Gold and Diamond Medallion Presented to Cubs Outfielder Billy Maloney
Awarded to Cubs outfielder W.A. “Billy” Maloney after the club’s victory over the Chicago White Sox in the 1905 City Series, this remarkable piece represents an early chapter in Chicago’s storied baseball rivalry. The postseason matchup, created in 1903 by White Sox owner Charles Comiskey and Cubs president James Hart, was designed to determine the true “Champion” of the Windy City. In total, 26 City Series were contested through 1942, each intensifying the competitive divide between Chicago’s two major league clubs.
Maloney (1882–1960) was a member of the Cubs during one of the most dominant stretches in franchise history. An outfielder known for his steady defensive play and dependable bat, Maloney lead the National League in stolen bases in the 1905 campaign, tying the Giants’ Art Devlin with 95.
To commemorate Maloney’s contribution to the Cubs’ 1905 City Series triumph, he was presented with this 14-karat gold medallion. The design incorporates Chicago’s familiar municipal “Y” device, symbolizing the branching of the Chicago River, accented by a baseball and crossed bats. At the Wolf Point intersection within the design rests a single old European-cut diamond weighing approximately 0.25 carat.
The reverse is engraved, “Presented to W.A. Maloney By National Commission.” Measuring just over one inch in diameter, the medallion stands as a tangible reminder of one of the earliest and most spirited chapters in Chicago baseball history.
Gross weight: 9.85 dwt. Accompanying chain is made of silver.

title: A Sept. 20, 1955 Rocky Marciano vs. Archie Moore World Heavyweight Championship Boxing Ticket – Final Bout of Marciano's Historic 49-0 Career
description_block:
A Sept. 20, 1955 Rocky Marciano vs. Archie Moore World Heavyweight Championship Boxing Ticket – Final Bout of Marciano's Historic 49-0 Career
Originally scheduled for September 20, 1955, the fight was postponed by one day due to inclement weather, making this ticket a tangible reminder of the drama that unfolded even before the first bell.
On September 21, 1955, World Heavyweight Champion Rocky Marciano faced the formidable Light Heavyweight Champion Archie Moore in a crowd of over 60,000 at Yankee Stadium.
In one of the most unforgettable nights in boxing history, Marciano was knocked down in the second round — only the second time in his career he would ever hit the canvas, before roaring back to floor Moore multiple times, ultimately winning by ninth-round knockout.
This night marked the final fight of Marciano’s illustrious career, a champion who would retire undefeated at 49-0, forever enshrined in boxing greatness.

title: A Rare Jostens 1985 Chicago Bears Super Bowl XX Championship Salesman Sample Ring Crafted to William "The Refrigerator" Perry's Size
description_block:
A Rare Jostens 1985 Chicago Bears Super Bowl XX Championship Salesman Sample Ring Crafted to William "The Refrigerator" Perry's Size
The 1985 season stands as one of the most memorable campaigns in professional football history. The Chicago Bears, powered by a defense widely considered among the finest ever assembled, dominated the league from start to finish. Their year culminated in a decisive 46–10 victory over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX, securing the franchise’s place in championship lore.
Rookie William “The Refrigerator” Perry added an unexpected chapter to the story. Primarily a defensive lineman, Perry was famously utilized in short-yardage situations on offense, where his touchdowns captured national attention and made him one of the season’s most talked-about figures.
Presented here is a scarce Jostens salesman’s sample of the championship ring crafted to Perry’s size. The substantial size 23 ring is fashioned in 10-karat gold, weighing approximately 30.74 pennyweights, and features an array of diamond simulants. Salesman’s samples of this caliber seldom surface, particularly examples produced to the proportions of one of the most iconic figures in Bears history.
As such, this offering represents an exceptional opportunity for collectors — a rare chance to acquire a tangible connection to one of the NFL’s most dominant and storied champions.

A 1990 Skybox Michael Jordan Signed Autograph Basketball Card No. 41 (PSA 9 MINT AUTO)
On February 17, 2023, as he turned 60, Michael Jordan marked the milestone in signature fashion by making history off the court. He donated a record-setting $10 million to Make-A-Wish America, the largest single gift the organization has ever received.
Jordan’s connection to Make-A-Wish stretches back to 1989, when he granted his very first wish. In the decades since, he has brought joy to children around the world, turning fleeting moments into lifelong memories.
One of those moments came on January 25, 1992. Before the Chicago Bulls defeated the Houston Rockets 114–100, Jordan took time to meet a young fan from Michigan in the Bulls’ locker room at Chicago Stadium. What followed wasn’t just a meet-and-greet, it was an unforgettable, deeply personal experience. The boy, battling Non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, spent time with his hero in a private autograph session, sharing cards and memorabilia that Jordan carefully signed.
Even amid game-day responsibilities, like distributing his allotment of tickets, Jordan remained fully present. He joked, laughed, and, most importantly, offered words of encouragement that left a lasting impact.
That encounter became more than a cherished memory. It became a source of strength. More than three decades later, the young boy is now a man who continues to win his fight.
Now, pieces of that extraordinary day – those signed cards, each authenticated and graded by PSA, are being shared with the collecting world, carrying with them a story of resilience, generosity, and the enduring power of a simple wish.

auction_title: Sale 6514 - Sports Memorabilia: Featuring The Baseball Card Collection of David Eisenhower
title: A 1906 Chicago Baseball Champions Gold and Diamond Medallion Presented to Cubs Outfielder Billy Maloney
description_block:
A 1906 Chicago Baseball Champions Gold and Diamond Medallion Presented to Cubs Outfielder Billy Maloney
Awarded to Cubs outfielder W.A. “Billy” Maloney after the club’s victory over the Chicago White Sox in the 1905 City Series, this remarkable piece represents an early chapter in Chicago’s storied baseball rivalry. The postseason matchup, created in 1903 by White Sox owner Charles Comiskey and Cubs president James Hart, was designed to determine the true “Champion” of the Windy City. In total, 26 City Series were contested through 1942, each intensifying the competitive divide between Chicago’s two major league clubs.
Maloney (1882–1960) was a member of the Cubs during one of the most dominant stretches in franchise history. An outfielder known for his steady defensive play and dependable bat, Maloney lead the National League in stolen bases in the 1905 campaign, tying the Giants’ Art Devlin with 95.
To commemorate Maloney’s contribution to the Cubs’ 1905 City Series triumph, he was presented with this 14-karat gold medallion. The design incorporates Chicago’s familiar municipal “Y” device, symbolizing the branching of the Chicago River, accented by a baseball and crossed bats. At the Wolf Point intersection within the design rests a single old European-cut diamond weighing approximately 0.25 carat.
The reverse is engraved, “Presented to W.A. Maloney By National Commission.” Measuring just over one inch in diameter, the medallion stands as a tangible reminder of one of the earliest and most spirited chapters in Chicago baseball history.
Gross weight: 9.85 dwt. Accompanying chain is made of silver.

against Spain, he scored 20 points in a decisive 96–65 victory.
For serious collectors, it is the ultimate pre-NBA Jordan collectible: a direct, tangible
connection to his first international dominance.

title: A Sept. 20, 1955 Rocky Marciano vs. Archie Moore World Heavyweight Championship Boxing Ticket – Final Bout of Marciano's Historic 49-0 Career
description_block:
A Sept. 20, 1955 Rocky Marciano vs. Archie Moore World Heavyweight Championship Boxing Ticket – Final Bout of Marciano's Historic 49-0 Career
Originally scheduled for September 20, 1955, the fight was postponed by one day due to inclement weather, making this ticket a tangible reminder of the drama that unfolded even before the first bell.
On September 21, 1955, World Heavyweight Champion Rocky Marciano faced the formidable Light Heavyweight Champion Archie Moore in a crowd of over 60,000 at Yankee Stadium.
In one of the most unforgettable nights in boxing history, Marciano was knocked down in the second round — only the second time in his career he would ever hit the canvas, before roaring back to floor Moore multiple times, ultimately winning by ninth-round knockout.
This night marked the final fight of Marciano’s illustrious career, a champion who would retire undefeated at 49-0, forever enshrined in boxing greatness.

title: A Rare Jostens 1985 Chicago Bears Super Bowl XX Championship Salesman Sample Ring Crafted to William "The Refrigerator" Perry's Size
description_block:
A Rare Jostens 1985 Chicago Bears Super Bowl XX Championship Salesman Sample Ring Crafted to William "The Refrigerator" Perry's Size
The 1985 season stands as one of the most memorable campaigns in professional football history. The Chicago Bears, powered by a defense widely considered among the finest ever assembled, dominated the league from start to finish. Their year culminated in a decisive 46–10 victory over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX, securing the franchise’s place in championship lore.
Rookie William “The Refrigerator” Perry added an unexpected chapter to the story. Primarily a defensive lineman, Perry was famously utilized in short-yardage situations on offense, where his touchdowns captured national attention and made him one of the season’s most talked-about figures.
Presented here is a scarce Jostens salesman’s sample of the championship ring crafted to Perry’s size. The substantial size 23 ring is fashioned in 10-karat gold, weighing approximately 30.74 pennyweights, and features an array of diamond simulants. Salesman’s samples of this caliber seldom surface, particularly examples produced to the proportions of one of the most iconic figures in Bears history.
As such, this offering represents an exceptional opportunity for collectors — a rare chance to acquire a tangible connection to one of the NFL’s most dominant and storied champions.
